articles.headline: ‘End game’: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce mocked by opponent
keyFacts: The Seattle Seahawks defeated the Kansas City Chiefs 20-3 on Sunday night, handing them their first loss of the season.
Following the victory, the Seahawks posted a Swift-themed friendship bracelet and the caption 'End Game' on social media to mock Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift.
With this loss, the Chiefs fell to a 5-1 record, leaving the Minnesota Vikings as the NFL's only remaining undefeated team.
body: Feb 11, 2024; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Recording artist Taylor Swift reacts during the first quarter of Super Bowl LVIII between Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports The Seattle Seahawks handed the Kansas City Chiefs their first loss of the season on Sunday night, and they made sure to rub it in afterward by trolling newlyweds Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift.

After their 20-3 win on Sunday Night Football , the Seahawks posted a Swift-themed troll on social media, sharing a friendship bracelet that spelled out “Seahawks Win.” And for the caption, they went with the title of one of Swift’s songs.
Seahawks Dominate Chiefs

Kansas City entered the night as one of the NFL’s last two undefeated teams, but Seattle’s defense shut the Chiefs down. Kansas City managed just 213 total yards and 11 first downs, and went 3-of-11 on third down in the 20-3 loss.

Mahomes completed 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards and an interception, and the Chiefs failed to reach the red zone for the first time in a game with Mahomes as their starting quarterback, according to Pro Football Talk . Kansas City’s three points were the fewest in a Mahomes start since 2021.
Meanwhile, Jaxon Smith-Njigba torched the Chiefs’ secondary for nine catches, 150 yards, and a touchdown.

Kelce got off to a slow start, failing to catch a pass in the first half. However, he finished the game with four catches for 44 yards, and moved into fifth place on the NFL’s all-time receptions list.
With the loss, Kansas City fell to 5-1, leaving the Minnesota Vikings as the NFL’s only undefeated team.
‘End Game’

After the game, the Seahawks wasted no time in trolling Swift and Kelce as the team’s official account posted a photo of a friendship bracelet reading “Seahawks Win.” The caption simply read, “End Game,” a reference to a song from Swift’s 2017 album reputation .
End Game https://t.co/fUGMpcCMjX
— Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) October 26, 2026
The bracelet is a nod to a tradition among Swift’s fans, who made and traded friendship bracelets at her Eras Tour concerts.

It’s also a nod to how Swift and Kelce got together. Kelce attended one of Swift’s shows in July 2023 and tried to give her a bracelet with his number on it, as ESPN noted . He wasn’t able to deliver it, but the two started dating a couple of months later, and they got married this past July.
Needless to say, Chiefs fans and Swifties probably didn’t find the joke very funny.

articles.headline: St. John’s men’s basketball wrangles Texas in encouraging exhibition finale
keyFacts: St. John's defeated seventh-ranked Texas 87-74 on Sunday afternoon in their final preseason exhibition game at Madison Square Garden.
Tounde Yessoufou, Ian Jackson, and Keyshawn Hall combined to score 65 of the Red Storm's 87 total points during the victory.
The Red Storm have eight days to prepare for their season opener against Monmouth on Monday, November 2.
body: Oct 25, 2026; New York, NY, USA; St. John's Red Storm guard Tounde Yessoufou (24) gestures after making a three point shot in the first half against the Texas Longhorns at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Although St. John’s survived last week’s four-overtime gauntlet against Rutgers with a win, they were unsatisfied with their performance and knew they needed to take massive strides to contend with seventh-ranked Texas in their final tune-up. They not only met the challenge, but also overdelivered.
The Red Storm ended their preseason on a high note with an 87-74 wire-to-wire win over the Longhorns on Sunday afternoon, proving they can outmatch the country’s best when their game clicks.
“I felt that we had to make a quantum leap from the Rutgers game,” Rick Pitino said on Sunday, “I was on them constantly on certain things, and they made a quantum leap today.”

St. John’s set the tone with active defense, turning ten Texas first-half turnovers into 14 points and holding the Longhorns to just 42.3% shooting before halftime. The Red Storm took the lead on a Tounde Yessoufou steal and breakaway layup at the 19:07 mark in the first half, and they held onto it for the remainder of the contest.
Tounde with the steal and score early 🔥 pic.twitter.com/9JN9RNTj66
— St. John's Men’s Basketball (@StJohnsBBall) October 25, 2026

Yessoufou, along with Ian Jackson and Keyshawn Hall, overwhelmed the Longhorns all day long. The offensively gifted trio showed off their firepower, scoring 65 of the Red Storm’s 87 total points and shooting 23-of-41 from the field (56 percent), and they shut down a Texas rally going into halftime by combining for a 12-0 run to send St. John’s into the break with a 49-31 lead. That margin ballooned to 22 points early in the second half.
“Every game is important to us; we want to show we can be connected, and today our play showed for itself,” Tounde Yessoufou told the media after the game.
The Baylor transfer showcased his two-way skill set with 23 points (8-of-14), five assists, and five steals, attacking the basket with authority and flexing his range with two made triples.
Tounde Yessoufou is an absolute DOG pic.twitter.com/YSp8lJ4W7A
— Cole Adams (@coleadamss) October 25, 2026

Ian Jackson put behind shoddy outings in the Red Storm’s previous two scrimmages and played with all sorts of control on Sunday, scoring 18 points (7-of-14), leading the Johnnies with three made triples, giving four assists, and hitting the glass for six rebounds, the second most of any Red Storm player. Rick Pitino considered Jackson’s performance the best he’s ever seen from the junior guard.
“He did all of the right things defensively; he didn’t force the offense,” Pitino said about Jackson after the game. “He just looked like a complete player in every phase of the game.”

As the Red Storm lost some gas as the game wound down, Keyshawn Hall buoyed the offense by posting 13 of his game-high 24 points in the second half. The self-described “big guard” shook off contact every time he went to the basket and established an air of toughness for the Johnnies.
Keyshawn AND 1 💪 pic.twitter.com/oDAu52K2nC
— St. John's Men’s Basketball (@StJohnsBBall) October 25, 2026
“We didn’t want to claw back into the game,” Hall said after the game. “We wanted to come out and set a standard to dominate on our home court in front of our fans.”

Those three carried the load offensively, but the Red Storm also got plenty of help inside from a promising freshman big man. Theo Edema made the most of his twelve minutes off the pine and showed his ready-made strength by pulling down a team-high seven rebounds, including four of the offensive variety, to help the Red Storm salt away this win.
The Red Storm have eight days to prepare for their season opener against Monmouth on Monday, November 2. Tip-off at Carnesecca Arena is scheduled for 6:30 p.m., and the game can be watched on ESPN+.

articles.headline: I tried Sonos’ clever new surround setup trick — and it delivers the home theater flexibility I’ve always wanted
keyFacts: Sonos introduced a new operating system feature that allows portable Play speakers to function as temporary rear home theater surrounds.
The reviewer reported that accelerometers and near-ultrasonic signals are used to automatically detect when speakers are moved or repositioned.
The reviewer stated that while automatic transitions occasionally required manual app adjustments, the setup successfully provided both surround sound and portable music functionality.
body: I've long been a fan of Sonos and its approach to home audio. My apartment is already filled with the company's speakers, including two home theater systems for movies and TV, and a couple of stereo pairs for music. And while the ability to group speakers and play whatever I want, wherever I want, is already a major part of the appeal, I've always felt there was room to take things a step further.

So when Sonos announced the Beam Ultra soundbar earlier this year, alongside a new feature that would allow its portable Play speakers to double as rear surrounds, my interest was well and truly piqued.

I've already made my feelings about the Play perfectly clear, having previously claimed it could be the only speaker you really need. Its ability to perform just as well around the home as it does on the move makes it an incredibly appealing proposition.

And now, thanks to the new Sonos27 operating system, that versatility extends to home theater. Rather than committing a pair of speakers to permanent surround duties, you can simply pick one up, take it into another room and use it independently, before returning it to its original position and having it automatically rejoin the system.

It's a simple idea, but one that has the potential to fundamentally change how people use their Sonos speakers. And having now put the Beam Ultra and a pair of Plays through their paces, I think it's one of the company's most compelling developments in years.
Play it for me, Sonos

A pair of Sonos Play speakers can be used as rear surrounds with several of the company's soundbars, including the Arc, Arc Ultra, Beam (Gen 2) and Beam Ultra. Given the larger size and greater output capabilities of the Arc models, I'd argue the relatively compact Plays might be a slight mismatch, but it's good to know you're not tied to one particular soundbar.

Pairing them with the smaller Beam makes more sense to me, and in my bedroom, the combination is discreet enough not to draw attention, yet powerful enough to deliver a genuinely expansive sound that's a huge improvement over my TV's built-in speakers.

Of course, the real appeal of this setup is that the Plays aren't permanently tied to surround duties. Pick one up, carry it into another room and it should automatically disconnect from the home theatre system, becoming an independent speaker ready for music playback. Return it to its original position, and it should seamlessly slot back into place.

Making this possible is some clever technology working behind the scenes. An accelerometer inside each Play detects when it's been picked up and moved, while Sonos Positioning Technology uses near-ultrasonic signals, picked up by the soundbar's microphones, to determine whether the speakers are in the same room and where they're positioned. It can even work out which speaker should act as the left or right rear surround, without you having to assign them manually.
At least, that's the theory.

When I first put this to the test, things didn't quite go according to plan. I carried one of the Plays from my bedroom into the living room, only to find it was still reproducing audio from the home theatre system. The connection also became intermittent, with the sound cutting in and out rather than the speaker switching to standalone mode.

I eventually resorted to tapping 'Stop Using Surrounds' in the Sonos app, which allowed me to use the Play independently. But when I returned it to the bedroom, it didn't automatically reconnect either, requiring another trip into the app to select 'Start Using Surrounds'.

Not wanting to be deterred, I tried again a short while later. This time, after moving the same Play into the living room and waiting a few seconds, I heard an audible tone confirming it had disconnected from the home theater setup. Both Plays, including the one still in the bedroom, then appeared as standalone speakers in my AirPlay settings.

Returning the speaker to its original position was just as straightforward. A breathing white light indicated it was determining its position relative to the soundbar, followed by the same audible tone confirming a successful connection. Just like that, it was back to performing rear-left surround duties, without me having to touch the app.

And that's when the appeal of Sonos' new approach really clicked. Instead of a pair of speakers permanently committed to home theater duties, I could now move them around my apartment as needed, without manually reconfiguring the system every time.
Small system, big sound
To give the system a proper workout and find out just how much the Play surrounds contributed, my first port of call had to be the Penguin car chase scene in The Batman.

I started with the Beam Ultra by itself and was, quite frankly, blown away by its performance. Considering the soundbar's compact dimensions, the sheer scale of the sound it produced was remarkable. The rumble of the Batmobile's engine had impressive weight, while the soundfield extended well beyond the physical confines of the bar. In fact, it effectively disappeared, with sound filling the room rather than appearing to come from a single speaker beneath the TV.

Perhaps more impressive was that I wasn't using a separate subwoofer. In my bedroom, at least, I didn't feel an immediate need for one, such was the weight and authority of the bass. Admittedly, a larger living room could tell a different story, and anyone craving particularly deep, room-shaking bass would likely benefit from adding a Sub Mini.

With the two Plays connected as surrounds, and both the surround and height audio settings left at their default level of 0, the performance became even more immersive. As Batman and Penguin sped along the highway, the sounds of passing lorries and cars extended behind my listening position, creating a more convincing sense of being in the middle of the action.

Curious to see how much further the system could go, I increased both the surround and height audio settings to +5. The presentation became even more enveloping, with rear-channel effects such as blaring car horns becoming easier to distinguish. And when Penguin's car went into a roll, the system did a convincing job of following the chaos unfolding on screen, making me feel as though I was right there in the passenger seat.
Arc you pleased to see me?

The Beam Ultra and Play combination had replaced an Arc and two Sonos Ones in my bedroom, so I was keen to see how the newer system compared with its predecessor. I reinstalled the older setup, starting with the Arc on its own.

There was an immediately noticeable increase in sheer grunt, which wasn't entirely surprising given the Arc's larger dimensions and greater number of drivers. But the difference wasn't quite as dramatic as I'd expected, particularly considering how much smaller the Beam Ultra is.

It was also a reminder of how much easier Sonos has made the process of adding portable surrounds. With the Plays, I could simply select 'Use Surrounds' and, within seconds, they would connect and automatically establish their left and right positions. The Ones required a more involved setup process, including manually assigning each speaker to its respective channel.
Returning to the same scene from The Batman, this time with the Ones connected, revealed a more substantial difference between the two systems.

The Arc-based setup produced a bigger, more authoritative sound, particularly with the surround TV level increased to +5. Car engines had greater low-frequency weight, while the movement of vehicles along the highway was easier to follow as sounds travelled around the room.

Where the Beam Ultra fought back was in its reproduction of higher frequencies and dialogue. Voices sounded clearer and more distinct than they did through the Arc, while effects such as screeching tyres had greater bite and definition.
And while I maintain that the Beam Ultra doesn't necessarily need a subwoofer in a smaller room, the comparison demonstrated that the Arc has an advantage when it comes to outright bass weight.

Ultimately, both systems delivered thoroughly enjoyable and convincing surround sound experiences. The Arc-based setup had the edge in scale and low-frequency authority, but the Beam Ultra and Plays proved that a relatively compact system can still deliver a seriously cinematic performance.
A home theater system with a difference

At $1,297 / £1,297/ AU$2,097 for the Beam Ultra and two Plays, this certainly isn't the cheapest way to bring surround sound into your home. In fact, Sonos' own Beam Ultra and Era 100 surround package costs less ($1,112 / £1,097 / AU$1,705), and as my comparison with the Arc and Ones demonstrated, a conventional setup can deliver a more substantial sound.
But I'd argue that focusing purely on the price of admission, or even outright surround performance, misses the point of what Sonos has achieved here.

Because when I'm not watching a movie or catching up on my favorite TV shows, I don't necessarily need two speakers sitting behind me doing nothing. With this setup, I can pick them up and take them wherever I please, whether that's into another room for some background music or outside for a gathering with friends.
And because the Plays offer both Wi-Fi and Bluetooth connectivity, they're just as comfortable being part of a multiroom Sonos system as they are accompanying me away from home.
In effect, I'm getting two systems in one: an immersive home theater setup when I want it, and a pair of genuinely portable wireless speakers when I don't.

For me, that's where the real value lies. Sonos hasn't just made its home theater systems more flexible; it's made the speakers themselves more useful. And having experienced how seamlessly the two roles can work together, it's a feature I'd find difficult to give up.

articles.headline: Lula is declared winner of Brazil’s election as Bolsonaro rejects results
keyFacts: Brazil’s electoral court announced that incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won reelection with 51.8% of the total vote.
Flávio Bolsonaro refused to concede defeat and asked for the election results to be annulled following voting extensions.
Lula is scheduled to begin his fourth non-consecutive term as president on January 5, 2027.
body: RIO DE JANEIRO (AP) — Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, a vocal critic of U.S. President Donald Trump, was reelected Sunday in a result that provides relief to critics of widening U.S. influence in Latin America .

With 100% of the vote counted, Brazil’s electoral court announced that the soon to be 81-year-old Lula had a lead of nearly 4.4 million votes over opponent Flávio Bolsonaro, giving him 51.8% of the total vote. Bolsonaro quickly refused to concede defeat and asked for the election results to be annulled after an evening of chaos at some polling places that followed a last-minute decision to extend voting by two hours.
Bolsonaro is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, whom Lula defeated to take the presidency in 2022.

Lula’s triumph bucks a regional trend of victories for right-of-center presidential candidates allied with Trump. It also means Latin America’s largest economy, with a GDP of $2.6 trillion per year, will likely continue defying Trump’s demands, despite the pressure of increased tariffs .
Lula says Brazil is ‘not anyone’s backyard’

A video published by Lula’s campaign shows the veteran leader celebrating with First Lady Rosângela da Silva and allies after his runoff victory was confirmed by Brazil’s electoral court. Wearing star-shaped red glasses, he kissed his wife.

Speaking to his supporters, thousands of whom gathered on Sao Paulo’s main artery and in Rio de Janeiro’s Cinelandia Square, Lula expressed his gratitude to the Brazilian people, and pledged to respect all Brazilians, regardless of gender or religion. He also attacked Bolsonaro.
“This was a defeat for denialism and lies. I must confess that every time I attended a debate, I felt embarrassed,” he said.
He also doubled down on his commitment to Brazil’s sovereignty.
“Either the homeland remains free, or we die for Brazil,” he said. “This country will not accept being anyone’s backyard.”

In Rio de Janeiro, cars beeped their horns and a woman dressed in red — the color of Lula supporters — shouted “You lost! Cry harder!” to four men in yellow and green sipping beers, Bolsonaro’s signature colors. A huge roar echoed in the street as the result was confirmed.

Rodrigo Valentim, a 51-year-old businessman and supporter of Bolsonaro, said that another Lula government would harm the economy. He pointed to financial markets’ positive reaction to the result of the first round, when Bolsonaro bested Lula.
“I don’t understand how people can vote for Lula,” he said. “The country is collapsing.”
Lula is set to begin his fourth non-consecutive term as president on Jan. 5, 2027.
Bolsonaro rejects results after confusion at polling places

The electoral court’s announcement ended an evening of confusion at polling places after Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin ruled three minutes before the scheduled end of voting to keep polls open for two more hours, following requests by both candidates. Lula’s request came after issues with buses that provide transportation to polls in Sao Paulo and Salvador, two cities that tend to favor the incumbent. Bolsonaro’s request was due to heavy rains in Brazil’s south, where he is favored.

The decision delayed tallying the votes by two hours. It was unclear how many polling stations stayed open after the scheduled closing time. Polling stations in Brasilia and Rio de Janeiro closed shortly after the original 5 p.m. deadline, reporters for The Associated Press observed.

Bolsonaro, whose father is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting a coup after he lost the 2022 presidential election to Lula, pointed out that Zanin is Lula’s former lawyer and criticized him for “changing the rules of the game in the middle of the game.”
“It’s impossible to recognize the results of the election in the context of these things that happened,” he said.

It’s not clear if Bolsonaro’s complaint could meet the legal threshold to annul the results. Bolsonaro also has the right to request a recount if he has evidence of fraud, but that might not change the results.
The president of the electoral court, Kassio Nunes Marques, who was appointed to the Supreme Court by former President Bolsonaro, said that the extension of voting hours did not impact results.

Joao Pedro Padua, a law professor at the Fluminense Federal University, said that Bolsonaro can file a lawsuit directly with the country’s electoral authorities or the Supreme Court, asking for the elections to be declared null and void.

“But there isn’t much legal basis for that,” Padua said. “The extension of voting hours is unusual, but for it to invalidate the elections, the candidate would have to prove that it affected voters’ ability to freely express their will. There doesn’t seem to have been any such impact.”
Lula overcame concerns about security and cost of living

Bolsonaro bested Lula by more than 2.2 million votes in the first round of the election earlier this month. Sunday night’s victory by Lula marked the first time since Brazil’s military dictatorship ended in 1985 that the second-highest vote-getter in the first-round elections won the presidency.

Lula faced a tough reelection battle because of concerns about the cost of living and security. Bolsonaro made a tough-on-crime approach the cornerstone of his campaign and pledged to bring down food costs while Lula, trying to lure undecided voters, has invested in costly incentives .

Both have been hit by corruption suspicions involving family members and allies, with Bolsonaro implicated in a sprawling scandal rocking Brazil. Lula previously spent more than a year in prison on corruption convictions that were eventually annulled .

This will likely be the last victory of the veteran leader’s political career. Lula began his political career in the 1970s as a union leader. He then helped found the Workers’ Party, which he represented as a presidential candidate three times until he finally won it in 2002. He was reelected four years later and was succeeded by one of his cabinet ministers, Dilma Rousseff, in 2010. She was reelected in 2014 but impeached two years later.

Lula tried to run for president again in 2018 but was jailed in March after being convicted. He was released from prison after 580 days and saw Brazil’s Supreme Court annul his sentence after police found messages that showed the judge who convicted him was biased. He quickly became one of Jair Bolsonaro’s biggest critics and narrowly beat him in 2022.

Since he lost the first round, Lula reorganized his campaign, appealed to young voters, put millions of Brazilians on the streets to defend democratic values and his legacy, raised fears of another Bolsonaro administration and boosted several government initiatives.
He joins Trump and Nicaragua’s President Daniel Ortega — all aged 80 — as one of the oldest presidents in the Americas.

articles.headline: US military says it helped Gulf states export 1.5 billion barrels of oil
keyFacts: US Central Command stated it helped Gulf nations export over 1.5 billion barrels of oil through the Strait of Hormuz since June.
Regional oil flows rebounded to pre-war levels of 16.5 million barrels daily in September despite Iranian threats, intelligence firm Kpler reported.
Commander Admiral Brad Cooper stated the US military remains focused on keeping commercial traffic flowing with regional partners.
body: US military forces have helped Gulf countries export more than 1.5 billion barrels of oil since June, despite Iran’s efforts to control the critical waterway, according to US Central Command (COMMAND).
The US military command said on Sunday that more than 3,000 commercial vessels had transited the Strait of Hormuz with its support over the past six months.

It added that more than 95 percent of ships navigating the channel had sailed through safely in recent months despite Iranian threats, “clearly demonstrating that the United States and regional partners control the international waterway”.

CENTCOM announced the figures as Commander Admiral Brad Cooper made a visit to the region, during which he observed the “current operational environment” in the strait while flying in a US Army helicopter.
“We continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with our Gulf partners and the shipping industry,” Cooper said in a statement.
“This visit underscores our strong commitment to continued freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.”
Cooper said the primary transit routes for vessels in the strait were free of Iranian mines due to the “incredible efforts” of personnel who conduct mine clearance operations.
“We remain intensely focused on keeping commercial traffic flowing as we work with our teammates in the US interagency, Gulf Cooperation Council, and shipping industry,” he said.

Crude oil flows have largely returned to levels seen before the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in late February, despite the ongoing threat of attacks on commercial vessels by Iranian forces.
At least 16.5 million barrels of oil per day left the region in September, equal to the pre-war average, excluding Iran, according to market intelligence firm Kpler.
Analysts have attributed the rebound to a combination of offshore ship-to-ship transfers, US military escorts, and increased use of oil pipelines.
However, oil prices remain far higher than before the start of the war.
Brent crude futures stood at about $114.50 a barrel on Sunday, after easing about 2 percent from last week’s nearly six-month high.
Brent settled at $72.48 per barrel on February 27, the day before the US and Israel began strikes on Iran.

articles.headline: Eric Bauza, The Voice Of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, And Many More Has Died At 46
keyFacts: Voice actor Eric Bauza has died suddenly at the age of 46, according to an announcement from his family.
Bauza was known as the modern voice of iconic Looney Tunes characters such as Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck.
His family announced his passing on Instagram on Sunday, October 25, stating that further details would be provided later.

articles.headline: Brazilian leftist President Lula wins reelection against conservative challenger Flavio Bolsonaro
keyFacts: Left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defeated conservative challenger Flavio Bolsonaro to win Brazil's presidential runoff with 51.7% of the vote, electoral authorities said.
Flavio Bolsonaro rejected his defeat, criticized a Supreme Court decision to extend voting hours, and announced plans to seek an annulment of the election results.
Several Latin American leaders congratulated Lula on his victory, while Lula vowed to resist US influence and pursue better regulation of big tech platforms.
body: What you need to know
- Left-wing incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defeated Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of the far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro
- It was a tight runoff, with Lula winning 51.7% of the vote against Bolsonaro’s 48.2%, official results showed
- In his victory speech, Lula urged more regulation of big tech platforms after allegations that Meta interfered in the race
- Several Latin American leaders congratulated Lula on win
- Bolsonaro refused to concede, calls for election results to be annulled

Flavio Bolsonaro rejects defeat, seeks annulment of Brazil election

Right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro has rejected his defeat to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Brazil’s presidential run-off, calling for the election to be annulled over a two-hour extension of voting hours.

Speaking to reporters after the electoral court declared Lula the winner, Bolsonaro said he could not accept the result. He criticized a decision by Supreme Court judge Cristiano Zanin to extend voting hours nationwide, arguing that it had changed the rules of the election.

"What happened today was not normal. It was unacceptable," Bolsonaro said, arguing that the nationwide extension had undermined equal treatment between states. He said he would take legal action against the result.

Lula’s campaign had requested the extension, citing difficulties transporting voters to polling stations in several states. Bolsonaro’s campaign had also sought extra voting time, but only in municipalities across five states, citing heavy rain, flooding and power outages.
Lula says Brazilians voted to defend democracy, vows to resist US influence
Brazilians voted to "guarantee democracy," President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said Sunday after beating Flavio Bolsonaro to win an unprecedented fourth term.

In a post on X, Lula thanked Brazilians, particularly young people who took to the streets in defense of democracy, saying: "This victory belongs to a people who believe, who fight, and who never give up on building a more just, sovereign, and democratic Brazil."

In his victory speech, Lula reiterated that Brazil would "not accept being anyone’s backyard," a recurring campaign message defending the country’s sovereignty against US influence. The stance may have helped him win votes, with some voters viewing Washington’s actions as interference.

Relations between the two countries deteriorated in 2025, when the US imposed tariffs on Brazil in retaliation for legal proceedings against former president Jair Bolsonaro, who was later convicted of coup-plotting.

Speaking in a hoarse voice, Lula thanked his campaign team and Brazilians, particularly young people who took to the streets to defend democracy. He described the result as a "loss for negativity, lies."
The re-elected president also promised better regulation of big tech platforms, after Meta was the subject of legal complaints over alleged "interference" throughout the polarizing campaign.
Latin American leaders congratulate Lula on election victory
Several Latin American leaders congratulated leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on his victory.
Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast said he had spoken to Lula and congratulated him, adding that "Chile and Brazil have a lot of shared future ahead."
Mexico’s left-wing President Claudia Sheinbaum congratulated Lula on his victory, writing on X: "Long live democracy, the people of Brazil won. Congratulations, President Lula!"
The presidents of Uruguay, Paraguay, Panama and Bolivia also congratulated Lula in posts on X.
Cuba’s president congratulated Lula on X, calling him "dear brother" and praising his victory as a win for peace, sovereignty and social justice.
IN PICTURES: Lula supporters celebrate, while Bolsonaro's fans disappointed
Brazil's Lula defeats conservative Flavio Bolsonaro in presidential election
Brazilian leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in office, defeating right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro in a presidential runoff, electoral authorities said.

Lula overcame his first-round defeat to Bolsonaro to secure victory in the runoff. The nearly 81-year-old leader won 51.7% of the vote, compared with 48.2% for Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.

The campaign was marred by scandals and mudslinging. Sunday’s vote was thrown into confusion after a last-minute Supreme Court ruling extended voting by two hours, following Lula’s claim that buses had been taken off the roads in several cities, preventing some voters from reaching polling stations.

Pollsters said higher-than-expected turnout appeared to have benefited Lula. Conservative candidates in Brazil typically lead early in the count, while left-wing candidates gain ground as votes from poorer, more populous northeastern states come in.

In regards to foreign policy in his next term, Lula will have to manage relations with Washington while maintaining his anti-imperialist stance, as the Trump administration increasingly asserts its influence across the region. Flavio Bolsonaro had campaigned on a promise of closer cooperation with Washington.

Around 159 million Brazilians were eligible to vote. Under Lula’s left-wing Workers’ Party, unemployment fell to a record low, poverty declined, the minimum wage rose and deforestation in the Amazon decreased. Congress also approved the gradual introduction of a five-day working week with two days off.

However, rising living costs, high public debt, Lula’s spending policies and a scandal involving alleged pension fraud weighed on his government. The economic challenges left many voters dissatisfied with his record and open to a return of the Bolsonaro family to power.

Lula finished the first round with 45% of the vote, two percentage points behind Flavio Bolsonaro. He became the first candidate since Brazil restored direct presidential elections in 1989 to overcome a first-round deficit and win the runoff.
The former trade unionist, who served as president from 2003 to 2010 before returning to office in 2023, now faces a challenging fourth term with a strong right-wing opposition.
Votes tallied in Brazil's presidential election after polls close
The electronic voting system used in the country means that a final result could be determined within a matter of hours, although that final result is expected to be tight.

Voting extended after complaints by both sides
Brazil's Supreme Court has moved to extend voting time in the presidential election until 7 p.m. local time (2200 GMT), giving voters an additional two hours.
The decision comes amid complaints from Lula's team that public bus services had been hampered, blocking people from getting to polling stations.
At the same time, Bolsonaro's team complained of weather conditions in certain regions making it more difficult for people to get out and vote.
Lula asks for polls to stay open longer after people 'barred from voting'
President Lula has requested an extension to poll opening hours after buses were taken out of circulation in Sao Paolo, the country's largest city, which he said prevented many people from voting.

"We are asking the Supreme Court to extend the electoral process so that those who were effectively barred from voting, due to the dirty tactics of mayors, can still cast their votes," Lula said, according to AFP.
Lula said 40% of buses in the city had been prevented from going into service, a claim that matched local media reports saying 75 buses had been blocked from leaving garages.
"I've never complained about anything in any election before. Whether I won or lost, I'd just accept it and get ready for the next one. But this time, something abominable is happening," he said.
"No one should give up on voting just because some scoundrel of a business owner or some crooked, criminal mayor tried to stop the people from casting their ballots."
Results show Brazilian voters in Germany back Lula
Brazilians in Germany have voted overwhelmingly for Lula, according to figures posted by Brazilian Embassies across the country and seen by DW's Portuguese service.
The left-wing incumbent, Lula, won 79.09% of the ballots cast by the 20,923 voters across Germany. This marks an increase on the 71.9% he won in the first round.
Brazilian voters in Germany could vote at embassies in Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt and Munich.

The German capital saw the greatest support for Lula, with 88.77% of the votes going his way. Frankfurt was the city with the greatest support for Bolsonaro, but on 29.03% he still trailed his opponent by some margin.

The turnout also increased in the second round in comparison to the first round when it stood at 19,322. However, for both rounds, only around half of the 41,552 eligible voters turned out to vote. Across the world, there are some 918,900 eligible voters for Sunday's election.
IN PHOTOS: Almost 160 million called out to vote
What role is Trump playing in Brazil's election?
Although he hasn't endorsed either candidate, US President Donald Trump is close to the Bolsonaro family.

Not only did the senior Bolsonaro imitate Trump's rhetoric and policies, he also refused to concede defeat after losing to Lula in 2022, leading to his imprisonment for an attempted coup, provoking comparisons with Trump's own defeat to Joe Biden in 2020.
On the other side, Lula has presented himself as a defense against US interference.
The right "wants to govern with the American flag," Lula said after casting his ballot on Sunday.
A Bolsonaro win would mark a further move in Latin America toward pro-US far-right leaders, following in the footsteps of countries such as Colombia, Chile and Peru.
Results expected within hours of polls closing

The president of Brazil's Superior Electoral Court, Kassio Nunes Marques, has said he expects the winner of Sunday's vote to be announced officially between 8.30 p.m. and 9 p.m. (2330 and 0000 GMT), according to A Folha de Sao Paolo.
Brazil uses an electronic voting system meaning that ballots can be tallied quicker than in elections where paper votes are counted by hand.
However, the gap between the winner and loser is expected to be small, with the two running head-to-head in pre-election polls.
Supreme Court president urges candidates to accept result of vote
The head of Brazil's Supreme Federal Court, Edson Fachin, has called for the candidates to respect the result of Sunday's vote.

"It's important to remember that all authority and power comes from the people and, thus, it is fundamental that the choices that derive from the manifestation of popular sovereignty are respected," he said as he left his local polling station, according to A Folha de Sao Paulo.
"Brazil needs peace and calm to, from tomorrow, be able to confront the major challenges in many areas that demand the presence of the state."
Some observers have posited that Flavio Bolsonaro could refuse to accept a Lula victory, like his father before him, with the potential for violence to erupt.

articles.headline: Cam Skattebo says he's going to keep breaking NFL rules after getting flagged for rarely enforced penalty
keyFacts: Giants running back Cam Skattebo was penalized for lowering his helmet during a game against the Houston Texans.
Skattebo stated after the game that he will not change his running style despite the penalty.
Continued penalties could create friction with coach John Harbaugh and cost the team 15 yards.
body: Cam Skattebo's running style might be illegal at times, but he's not going to change his ways. The Giants running back delivered a huge game in New York's 26-21 overtime win over the Houston Texans, but he sparked some controversy early in the game.

During the first quarter, Skattebo got called for one of the most surprising penalties of the week. The Giants running back got flagged for a rarely enforced unnecessary roughness, with the officiating crew ruling that he had lowered his helmet to draw contact.

The 15-yard penalty was surprising because officials don't usually flag an offensive player for lowering their helmet. Heading into Week 7, they had only thrown four penalty flags all season for lowering their helmets, and only one of those came against an offensive player. That other player was Houston's Foster Moreau, but he was flagged for making a tackle on a punt return in Week 2, so Skattebo is the only player to have been penalized while playing offense.

On one hand, Skattebo was bound to get penalized at some point because he's a human battering ram who seeks out contact with defensive players. Despite his running style, this was the first time in his career that he had ever been flagged for lowering his helmet, but it might not be his last.
Following the game, the Giants running back was asked whether he might change his running style to avoid future penalties, and apparently, he's not planning to change anything.

"The NFL loves to post me when I do stuff like that but then also wants to take stuff from me," Skattebo said in his postgame comments. "I'm going to run the ball like I want to run the ball. If I'm going to continue to get flags for it or fined for it, guess I'm going to play for free."

In layman's terms, Skattebo is still planning to truck over defenders whenever he has the ball. The problem with this plan is that there's a good chance Giants coach John Harbaugh won't like it. Now that Skattebo has been penalized, officials will likely be on the lookout for him to possibly lower his head going forward, and if he gets flagged, it will cost the Giants 15 yards.

If Skattebo continues to get flagged because he's unwilling to change his ways, that will almost certainly draw the ire of Harbaugh, which is not what the running back needs, because he's already been in the doghouse this year. He had zero touches in Week 6, but he made up for that with a huge game against the Texans, rushing .
If Skattebo doesn't want to end up back in Harbaugh's doghouse, he'll probably need to slightly adjust his running style so he doesn't get flagged going forward.

articles.headline: El Sayed mocks Rogers’s ‘earpiece’ and Trump’s ‘a**’ remarks in Grand Rapids rally
keyFacts: Abdul el Sayed mocked Republican Senate rival Mike Rogers and President Donald Trump during a Sunday rally in Grand Rapids, Michigan.
El Sayed criticized Rogers for appearing to lose an earpiece during a television interview and made fun of Trump's recent comments.
Sen. Bernie Sanders campaigned for el Sayed as both political parties brought national figures to Michigan in the final stretch of the Senate race.
body: GRAND RAPIDS, Michigan— Abdul el Sayed turned his Sunday rally appearance with Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) into a roast of his Republican Senate rival Mike Rogers and President Donald Trump.

El Sayed mocked Rogers for appearing to lose his earpiece during a Sunday morning television interview after Kristen Welker of NBC’s Meet the Press asked the former congressman whether a vote for him would amount to a vote for Trump’s agenda.
“After answering all of these questions just fine, he’s like, ‘I’m so sorry I lost my earpiece. What did you ask?’” el Sayed said, prompting laughter from the Grand Rapids crowd.
Michigan Senate candidate Abdul el Sayed roasts President Donald Trump at Grand Rapids, Michigan, rally on Oct. 26, 2026. (Barnini Chakraborty/Washington Examiner)
El Sayed then said he would answer the question for Rogers.
“Yes, a vote for Mike Rogers is a vote for Donald Trump’s agenda,” he said. “It always has been. It always will be.”
The jab came as Trump was campaigning with Rogers at a rally in Port Huron, where the president made a comment about rapper Nicki Minaj’s backside.
El Sayed seized on that, too.
“For whatever reason, this is like the third campaign stop in a row where Donald Trump can’t mention, can’t help but mention somebody’s a**,” he said. “You see that?”
The crowd laughed as el Sayed joked he would have to keep Trump away from him if he makes it to Washington.
El Sayed then pivoted back to the substance of the Senate race, telling voters to treat Trump as if he were on the ballot.

“I want everybody to vote like Donald Trump is on the ballot,” he said. “Because, friends, Donald Trump is on the ballot. Donald Trump’s war in Iran is on the ballot. Your gas prices are on the ballot. Your grocery prices are on the ballot. The ability to see a doctor is on the ballot.”
El Sayed also returned to a line from his recent debate with Rogers, when the Republican candidate said, “The last three years have been amazing.”
“For Donald Trump, he made $2.2 billion,” el Sayed said. “The last two years for him have been amazing.”
Rogers, he added, “sits on $14 million and counting.”
El Sayed continued referencing the two as a pair, saying: “So for Mike Rogers and Donald Trump, the last two years have been amazing. How about you, Grand Rapids?”
TRUMP: NICKI MINAK HAS ‘ONE HELL OF A BEAUTIFUL A**’
Sanders is campaigning for el Sayed in the final stretch of the Michigan Senate race as Democrats seek to hold the open seat being vacated by retiring Sen. Gary Peters (D-MI).

The rally came on a weekend when both parties brought national star power to Michigan: Trump campaigned for Rogers in Port Huron, and Sanders made the case for el Sayed in Grand Rapids, a day after former President Barack Obama stumped for the Democratic candidate in Detroit.

articles.headline: Steam Week in Review: AI disclosures enter the discourse again, as Epic CEO calls them 'just as partisan as mandatory political essays'
keyFacts: Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney criticized Valve on X for requiring mandatory AI disclosures on Steam, calling the policy a partisan political tool.
Valve implemented the AI disclosure requirement to manage legal and developmental risks due to the high volume of games released on Steam.
Valve is not anti-AI, as co-founder Gabe Newell previously supported OpenAI financially in its infancy.
body: Valve's mandatory AI disclosures are once again at the centre of the discourse, mostly thanks to Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, who has long been vocally against them. The debate has been reheated in the same month Epic Games proudly announced it will pivot to "AI first" development on its forthcoming Star Wars and Marvel crossover. Then it announced an AI game jam, before walking back its requirement for AI to be used.

But the true battleground has been on Elon Musk's X, where Sweeney's refocused his reticule on Steam. One of his most repeated notions this time around is that forcing developers to disclose AI use is inherently political.

"Forcing developers to write a political statement to be used against them by the hate mob they're [Valve is] helping organize is abhorrent," he wrote on October 24 in response to some AI loving guy who works at an AI company.

Later, to another user: "These AI statements are just as partisan as mandatory political essays or forcing developers to list their voting history to drive cancel campaigns and public struggle sessions."

And then: "There is a real economic cost to Valve’s foray into forced political disclosures. Besides taking 30%, they’re also taking a potentially even larger fraction of developers’ revenue and livelihood by undermining their business with these AI hate campaigns."
(Later, when a user wrote this is a "big opening for Epic if Valve doesn't figure this out", Sweeney replied "Yep!")

On October 25: "They [Valve] are burning down the businesses of good developers to enforce their politics. A year from now they’ll all be using AI, games will be better and made faster, and they’ll pretend their hate mob posting the death threats wasn’t wrong but merely misunderstood."
From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

In Valve's defence—and I rise in Valve's defence trepidatiously—the AI disclosure was initially imposed due to a seeming uncertainty with how use of this "legally murky" technology was unfolding in the game dev space. "Today's changes are the result of us improving our understanding of the landscape and risks in this space, as well as talking to game developers using AI, and those building AI tools," Valve wrote at the time. "This will allow us to be much more open to releasing games using AI technology on Steam."
"We'll continue to learn from the games being submitted to Steam, and the legal progress around AI, and will revisit this decision when necessary."

Why didn't Epic Games Store do the same? I'm not taking a swipe at EGS here, easy as it may be, but Epic Games' shopfront publishes a tiny slither of what Valve's does. In 2024, 1,100 games were released on EGS. Steam's figure was 18,433. Given that volume and the "legally murky" environment, the AI disclosure starts to look a whole lot more sensible.

Leaving aside whether insisting on AI disclosures in 2026 is inherently political—and I'm not denying it is, if inadvertently—Sweeney's posts on X do labour to imply that Valve is an anti-AI company taking a steadfast anti-AI stance, which, manifestly, it is not. Gabe Newell himself was an enthusiastic supporter of OpenAI in its infancy, donating $20 million to the then nonprofit enterprise. His most recent public comments on AI are not unlike those made by very many other enthusiastic tech billionaires, albeit less hyperbolic. That Valve will refresh its AI disclosure requirement in the medium to long term future seems inevitable to me.
But I do wonder what Sweeney dislikes more: anti-AI sentiment, or Steam?

It's an unusual time for him to revive this debate with such vigor. We are living through peak slop. The majority of games that release on Steam every week are irredeemable. The latest Claude model is facilitating the rapid thieving of game concepts and even code. Graphical assets, in-game music, in-game voices, generated using AI, immediately signal their provenance and are ugly as hell.

I don't doubt AI use in game dev will increase, but it will probably need to tend sharply away from the sensorial. Optimistically, most serious developers will realise that the vast majority of us don't want to see or hear that shit. I suspect that for most people, anti-AI sentiment, at least where games are concerned, isn't principled: it's a visceral emotional response.
Top Steam games by revenue (October 13 - 20)

Modern Warfare 4's official release date was October 23: its placement here is thanks to a pre-order incentive granting early access to the campaign. It's not a bad result, obviously, but I'm surprised it didn't topple PUBG. COD games do seem more spiritually at home on console, I guess.

Enshrouded hit 1.0 after a stint in early access, hence its reappearance here. Of particular note is something not shown in the above list: Over the Hill, the chillaxed offroading sim by the creators of Art of Rally, hit number 11 on the revenue charts for this period. That's a damn good result, and well deserved.

To provide a little bit more (slightly random) context: the new Castlevania game, which released on the same day as Over the Hill, came in at number 15. It's surprising that an offroading game would outperform a new entry in one of the medium's most beloved series. But then: the Snowrunner and Mudrunner games are extremely popular.
Last week's Steam deep cuts
Grease Trap '99 | October 22

A first-person PSX-style survival horror, yet again set in a retail environment. Except Grease Trap '99 is all about living "the Scottish dream", and creator James Muirhead takes his theme seriously: the voice acting here in in Scottish Gaelic. Despite being yet another shop keep horror, Grease Trap '99 doesn't take itself entirely seriously, and is also meant to make you laugh.
Family Manners | October 24

Here's a deeply weird artefact about the seemingly run-of-the-mill Evans family. Mr Evans arrives home one day from work one day to find things strangely unsettled in his home. What's going on? Maybe you don't want to know. This is a one hour narrative-driven affair where "fear gradually builds through psychological horror and mystery".
Interregnum | October 26

Though Interregnum was made for Commodore 64 and runs in the Vice C64 emulator, I don't actually think it ever existed back in the '80s and '90s: this is, as far as I can tell, a brand new turn-based strategy game for the platform. Details are thin, save for that it supports up to four players locally, but it sure looks gorgeous if you've got a fondness for ye olde personal computing.
Moadra | October 22

This came out of no where: a horror-tinged sci-fi metroidvania with an art style vaguely reminiscent of HR Giger's Alien work. The format is extremely familiar: explore a sprawling interconnected world, fight stuff, gain new abilities, get lost etctera. But Moadra genuinely has a look of its own.

Shaun Prescott is the Australian editor of PC Gamer. With over ten years experience covering the games industry, his work has appeared on GamesRadar+, TechRadar, The Guardian, PLAY Magazine, the Sydney Morning Herald, and more. Specific interests include indie games, obscure Metroidvanias, speedrunning, experimental games and FPSs. He thinks Lulu by Metallica and Lou Reed is an all-time classic that will receive its due critical reappraisal one day.

articles.headline: ‘We’re not doing great’: Gilgeous-Alexander in tears after Williams suffers gruesome leg injury
keyFacts: The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the Los Angeles Clippers 108-101 on Sunday night to remain undefeated.
Thunder guard Jalen Williams suffered a serious left leg injury late in the game and left the court on a stretcher.
Thunder coach Mark Daigneault stated that the team would receive an update on the injury on Monday.
body: Shai-Gilgeous Alexander scored 34 points and the Oklahoma City Thunder stayed undefeated but they lost All-Star guard Jalen Williams to what appeared to be a serious leg injury during their 108-101 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday night.

Oklahoma City won their third straight game to start the season but lost three players to injury, including Williams, who went down hard on a drive to the basket with 1:14 left. The guard’s left leg gave way as he landed and his foot bent at an unnatural angle. The 25-year-old left the court on a stretcher with towels covering his injured leg. He covered his mouth with his hands when he looked down at the injury while Gilgeous Alexander and players on both teams appeared to be in shock.
“We’re not doing great,” Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said after the game. He added that the team would be updated on the injury on Monday.
Gilgeous-Alexander was in tears as he spoke about Williams after the game.

“I just feel bad for him,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “It’s obviously going to be tough without a player like that. But he’s not gone for ever. He’ll be back better than ever, and we know it. We’ve just got to hold the fort down until he comes back.”
Williams missed 49 games last season due to a variety of injuries but was a key part of the Thunder’s title campaign in 2025.
Thunder guard Cason Wallace (left shoulder soreness) and forward Jaylin Williams (right wrist soreness) left the game in the first quarter and did not return.

articles.headline: Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado returns after months in exile
keyFacts: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela after more than 10 months in exile, as confirmed by her allies and photographs on Sunday.
Machado's return followed her previous departure in January to accept the Nobel Peace Prize, after which US forces removed her opponent, President Nicolás Maduro.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Machado's safe return resulted from US-supported reconciliation talks that also freed political prisoners.
body: - Published
Venezuelan opposition leader MarÃa Corina Machado has returned home to a fraught political landscape after more than 10 months in exile.
"I am here. With you," Machado wrote on X on Sunday. Her return comes after repeated prior efforts to re-enter the country came to no avail.
In January, a month after Machado left Venezuela on a speedboat under cover of darkness to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway, the US seized her opponent, President NicolÃ¡s Maduro.
The Trump administration then backed his deputy, Delcy RodrÃguez, as leader and she was sworn in as interim president, later signing an oil deal which granted very favourable terms to the US.
Machado was photographed on Sunday attending Mass at a church in the Venezuelan state of Lara, surrounded by supporters hugging her and clasping her hands.
She then began travelling to the capital Caracas in a caravan of cheering supporters. More supporters have lined the route of her journey to the capital.
She was photographed smiling as she leaned out of the sunroof of a car as she entered Caracas late on Sunday night.

Her ally, former presidential candidate Edmundo GonzÃ¡lez, confirmed her arrival, writing in a statement: "I am thrilled to announce to you that our leader, my dear MarÃa Corina, is on Venezuelan soil."
"Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!" GonzÃ¡lez said.
He added that he will soon join Machado in Venezuela to advance the country "toward freedom".

An advisor to Machado said in September that over the previous few weeks Machado had attempted seven times to return to Venezuela, but was denied each time. There have been reports that the US was involved in delaying her return, which it has denied.

It's unclear what Machado plans to do next now that she's back, but she has previously said she would run for president again if an election were held. Her ability to return to her country was always contingent on approval from the Trump administration, which it appears has now been granted.

A staunch supporter of democracy, Machado won an independent presidential primary election - held outside the Maduro government's official election authority - in 2023, earning more than 90% of the vote.

Despite winning the primary, Maduro's government barred Machado from running for office, accusing her of fraud and tax violations. Machado denied the allegations, calling them politically motivated. She spent her final days in the country hiding in safehouses before her fleeing to Norway to accept the Nobel Prize.
In the 2024 election, Machado's ally GonzÃ¡lez ran in her place against Maduro.
The electoral authority, which is closely aligned with the government, declared Maduro the winner without making detailed voting tallies public.
The opposition argued that GonzÃ¡lez won the election, not Maduro, uploading copies of the voting tallies as evidence.
Maduro was removed from the country by US forces in January, and is currently jailed in New York where he faces drugs, weapons and torture charges. He has pleaded not guilty.
A spokesman for Machado called her return "a major step toward a democratic transition and free, fair, and verifiable presidential elections in the near future".

"We thank President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the US Government, Congress, and allied governments for their continued leadership and support," her spokesperson, David Smolansky, added.
Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Trump said, "I don't know anything about" her return, and added that he hoped she was "safe".
"I think she's a very nice woman. She gave me her Nobel Prize, so how can I say anything else? And I hope she's safe," he said.
In January, Machado visited the White House and gifted her Nobel prize award to Trump. The committee that issues the prize had said "it cannot be revoked, shared, or transferred to others".
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio praised his country's role in securing her return through political reconciliation talks.

"The conditions allowing for the safe return of Ms Machado to Venezuela is the direct result of the US supported reconciliation talks which has already seen hundreds of political prisoners freed and hundreds of political opposition figures return from exile," he posted on X.

He added: "We expect all political actors to support these talks which represent the best chance Venezuela has had in thirty years to peacefully achieve not just a free and fair election but an enduring democracy."

articles.headline: The 10 Best SNES Games to Play on Nintendo Switch Online
keyFacts: Polygon published a list of the 10 best Super Nintendo games available to play through Nintendo Switch Online.
The curated selection features first-party Nintendo classics like Super Mario World, Super Metroid, and EarthBound.
The article notes that many notable third-party titles, such as Chrono Trigger and Final Fantasy 6, are missing from the service.
body: The Super Nintendo Entertainment System has one of the finest game catalogs of any console ever released, and there's a strong selection of 77 games available on Nintendo Classics as part of Nintendo Switch Online. Sadly, most of the console's great third-party games aren't represented; you won't find Chrono Trigger, Final Fantasy 6, or Street Fighter 2 Turbo on the service.

But it doesn't really matter, because you will, of course, find many of Nintendo's own games — and these represent an incredible golden age for the studio, when Shigeru Miyamoto and Takashi Tezuka's teams were pumping out masterpiece after masterpiece. It's one of the best runs any game developer has ever had, a time of perfection between the innovation of the NES before and the bold leap into 3D with the N64 that came after.
Here are the 10 best SNES games you can play on Nintendo Classics.
1 Mario Paint

Nintendo loves to put together oddball game-and-accessory bundles, and in 1992 it sold a mouse for the SNES with this delightful art creation suite. There are funny minigames, brilliant tunes, authentic Nintendo sprites to use, as well as drawing, animation, and music creation suites. You'll need a USB mouse to play it on Switch, but Switch 2 owners can use the Joy-Con 2 in mouse mode.
2 Kirby Super Star

Smash Bros. director Masahiro Sakurai's restless imagination and love of remixes and mash-ups can be found as far back as this barmy 1996 anthology platformer. Kirby Super Star is a compilation of compressed ideas and stories expressed through the medium of the ability-copying pink blob: a racing game, a Metroidvania, a boss rush, scrolling shmup levels, and various rule variations on the classic platformer. It’s a glorious, throwaway blizzard of ideas, perfect for dipping into.
3 Donkey Kong Country 2: Diddy's Kong Quest

Rare's SNES platform game trilogy was visually flabbergasting at the time, and its rendered technique and huge sprites still look unique now. They can't compare with the in-house Nintendo platformers of the time for sophistication and invention, but they're slick, stuffed with secrets, and have amazing soundtracks and ambiance. Of the three games, Diddy's Kong Quest is surely the best.
4 Panel de Pon

Known as Tetris Attack in the West — where Nintendo of America jazzed it up with characters like Yoshi and a rather spurious application of the Tetris licence — Panel de Pon is an immaculate match-three puzzle game made by Intelligent Systems (Advance Wars, Fire Emblem). There's nothing fancy about it, it's just brilliant, endless block-matching action for one or two players.
5 EarthBound

The SNES was home to so many great RPGs, it's a shame there aren't more of them on Nintendo Switch Online. But we do have this gloriously kooky cult classic from Shigesato Itoi and Satoru Iwata, which uses a traditional RPG framework to explore a satirical, child's-eye-view world of contemporary Americana, alien invasions, and murderous taxi cabs.
6 Super Mario Kart

This incredibly influential 1992 racing game invented and perfected a whole genre at the first try. It's stunning how all the key components of what became a world-conquering series are present here, but also how different Super Mario Kart is from what the series became; with its tight track layouts and grippy handling, it's more precise and technical. It’s also brilliant in head-to-head two-player mode.
7 Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island

The supposed sequel to Super Mario World is really anything but; it's the first Yoshi game instead, as well as one of the funniest, loveliest things Nintendo has ever made. With graphics made of crayon scribbles and splashes of watercolor, stretchy, wobbly physics courtesy of the Super FX chip, and wild slapstick gameplay that just never stops rocking, Yoshi's Island is a gorgeous, irreverent hymn to innocence.
8 Super Metroid

Super Metroid is, quite simply, the Metroid game. It might even be the Metroidvania. Fabulously atmospheric and labyrinthine, this game captures better than any other — even the first Metroid Prime — the series' lonely, obscurely threatening sci-fi futurism.
9 The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past

After the dead-end detour of Zelda 2: Link's Adventure, the third Zelda game returned to the original's top-down layout, tempered its brutal mystery, and found a formula that would work for the next 25 years: an intricate clockwork fable of beautifully interlocking parts built around a stunning conceit — in this case, a dark mirror-world – that turns the game inside out and upside down. Miyamoto and Tezuka turned this game out less than a year after they made Super Mario World. Nobody's ever done it better.
10 Super Mario World

The SNES' launch game is its best game, which is saying something considering the competition. It's also — sorry, Super Mario Bros. 3 fans — the best 2D Mario game, hands down. There's Yoshi, there's the power-ups, there's the way the series' trademark surreal non-sequiturs are somehow braided, more convincingly than ever before or since, into a contiguous universe so gloriously silly and strange you can only marvel at it. Platforming perfection.

articles.headline: Bruce Blakeman calls Kathy Hochul Zohran Mamdani's 'puppet' during New York campaign rally
keyFacts: Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman called Governor Kathy Hochul a puppet of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a campaign rally.
Blakeman accused Hochul of embracing the mayor's agenda and failing to address illegal immigration and crime during the event.
Hochul and Mamdani have been campaigning together to emphasize policies focused on affordability and child care for working families.
body: Republican New York gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman blasted Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul as a "puppet" of New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a campaign rally Sunday.

Speaking at the event in Yorktown Heights, New York, Blakeman, the current Nassau County executive, accused his opponent of embracing the democratic socialist mayor's agenda while failing to crack down on illegal immigration and crime.
"Kathy Hochul, she was out campaigning with Mamdani this week," Blakeman said, according to the New York Post . "And I say that’s great."

"Please take him everywhere you go, Kathy, because I want to remind people that this un-American, antisemite, anti-Christian mayor is running the Democratic Party and Kathy Hochul is nothing more than his puppet," he continued.
HOCHUL DEFLECTS WHEN PRESSED ON TIES TO 'ANTI-CHRISTIAN' MAMDANI IN FIERY DEBATE MOMENT: 'SHAME ON YOU'
Hochul has been campaigning alongside Mamdani, including at a recent rally in Brooklyn.
The political alliance between the mayor and the governor, who is seeking reelection to a second full term, comes as democratic socialists have gained greater influence in New York politics.

Along with Mamdani's victory in last year's mayoral election, candidates aligned with Mamdani and New York's democratic socialist movement scored major victories in congressional primaries this year, including the defeats of two Democratic incumbents.
Blakeman has previously targeted Hochul and Mamdani over public safety, accusing both Democrats of failing to address crime in New York City.
FAR-LEFT SURGE: MAMDANI-BACKED CANDIDATES OUST DEM ESTABLISHMENT INCUMBENTS
During a campaign appearance on the city's subway system earlier this month, Blakeman described Hochul as the "most pro-criminal governor" and accused both leaders of failing to keep commuters safe.
Mamdani has also publicly criticized Blakeman, accusing the Republican gubernatorial candidate of engaging in "bigotry and racism" following a debate between Blakeman and Hochul earlier this month.

"I think the governor did a good job," Mamdani told reporters when asked about Hochul's response to Blakeman's criticism. "And I'll never fault someone for not being able to catch all of it because that is a fool's errand when it comes to Bruce Blakeman."
Hochul and Mamdani have emphasized affordability and child care while campaigning together, arguing their policies are aimed at lowering costs for working families.
Fox News Digital has reached out to Hochul's and Mamdani's offices for comment.
Fox News Digital's Eric Mack and Anders Hagstrom contributed to this story.

articles.headline: LA’s top federal prosecutor scorches California after noncitizen voters battle
keyFacts: The Department of Justice and California faced off in a federal appeals court regarding 20,000 voters the federal government claims are noncitizens.
Federal prosecutors argued that California must set aside these votes to protect election integrity, while state officials maintained the federal government lacks intervention authority.
The three-judge panel adjourned without an immediate ruling and questioned whether the court has the jurisdiction to issue an injunction while the election is underway.
body: Bill Essayli said he was concerned noncitizen votes were already being counted across the state, with the processing of mail-in ballots having started on Saturday ahead of the November 3 elections.
He made the claim after an extraordinary court hearing Sunday where the Department of Justice faced off with California over 20,000 voters who the federal government claims are noncitizens.

Speaking after the court adjourned on Sunday, Essayli told The Post: “Our concern is that noncitizens are actively voting in this election and California has confirmed they will count their votes. This will corrupt the integrity of the upcoming midterm election.”

Thanks for signing up!
The DOJ has demanded the state set these votes aside while California officials claimed the federal government had no right to make such an intervention when the election was already underway.

The three judges in the case appeared sympathetic toward the state’s argument, with them unsure whether they had the jurisdiction to force the ballots to be put aside — but they adjourned without a ruling as of Sunday afternoon.

“I think it’s absolutely incredible that California just walked into a room with the United States government and said these votes should be counted in the elections,” Essayli said. “They argued that whether or not they are noncitizens is irrelevant. It dilutes the votes of American voters.”
“We are committed to fighting this because even one noncitizen vote is one too many. They seem completely disinterested in the fact they are tabulating votes from noncitizens,” he added

Meanwhile the DOJ sent letters to every county in the state requesting local election officials to help identify any noncitizen voters and gave them 48 hours to comply. It also sued California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder Dean Logan on Oct. 15.

The hearing renewed calls for voter ID in California’s elections, with Prop 39 coauthor Carl DeMaio telling The Post that voters have been “lied” to about the current levels of citizenship verification before ballots are counted.

DeMaio told The Post the noncitizen voters discovery shows the state has shown a “dereliction of duty.” “And now that that truth is out there, I think that the voters need to understand that the politicians will not do a proper review of citizenship. They are not doing their job,” he said. “They’re putting people in legal jeopardy. And as a result, Prop 39 is needed more than ever because, we have to force the politicians to do their job at the ballot box.”
California gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton weighed in: “This is typical of everything that’s been going wrong in California. We’ve got a bunch of people in charge who just wont enforce the law.”

Essayli’s comments came just a day after a tense back and forth on X with Gov. Gavin Newsom, who blasted the DOJ’s attempts as a desperate “clown show” — but the top federal prosecutor quipped back: “Hey Fraud King. We’re not waiting for them to vote. You’re not allowed to have any noncitizens on your voter rolls. ‘Period. Full stop.'”

The Sunday afternoon hearing was held before a three-judge federal appeals panel, including two Trump-appointed judges, that grilled the Justice Department over its bid to have the 20,000 votes set aside.

“It seems to me that you want us to issue an injunction that is entirely inconsistent with the law,” Judge Mark Bennett, a Trump appointee, told Justice Department attorney Matthew Donnelly. “How can we do that?”
During the hearing, two of the three Ninth Circuit judges suggested the court may lack the authority to intervene because a lower-court judge has a hearing scheduled for Tuesday.

As of Sunday afternoon the panel had not ruled but said it would decide the matter “as quickly as possible.” If it dismisses the appeal, the case will return to US District Judge David O. Carter in Santa Ana on Tuesday.

“Once a mail-in vote is processed, it cannot be unprocessed, and the damage is irreversible and irreparable,” Donnelly said, noting Los Angeles County had estimated it processed more than 500,000 ballots.
Judge Gabriel Sanchez, a Biden appointee, pressed the DOJ on unnamed “third party analytics” used to compile the 20,000-strong list of suspected noncitizens.
Donnelly pointed to sworn declarations from two Department of Homeland Security employees vouching for the process.

Sanchez also asked why a July letter from DHS to Weber had cited about 190,000 potentially problematic registrants. “So what changed in the intervening months to go from 190,000 to 20,000?” he asked. Donnelly said the drop came from DHS’s vetting process. He said the July figure came from a list that had not yet been through that review, because DOJ was hoping California would cooperate.
Sanchez, who appeared skeptical of the appeal, noted that ballot envelopes carry only a name, address and signature, not identifying details such as Social Security numbers.
“My name is Gabriel Sanchez. I guarantee you there are many Gabriel Sanchezes in the county of Los Angeles,” he said, questioning how officials could reliably match names to ballots.
“The United States executive is unhappy with what [California] is doing and doesn’t like the manner in which they have determined how they’re going to conduct the election,” Bennett said.
“But it seems to me that under the Elections Clause, they have the right to determine the manner of the elections, including sorting out noncitizens.”
“How can we, a federal court, do what is reserved to Congress, which Congress, in my view, hasn’t done?” Bennett asked.
The third judge, Trump appointee Patrick Bumatay, appeared more sympathetic to the DOJ, pressing California on whether it could identify noncitizen voters.
He said: “Without an injunction, you will never know, correct? Because if the ballots are cast and separated, then they’re going to be tabulated, and there’s no way of knowing.”

Sam Siegel, arguing for California, replied: “Your Honor, we would respectfully disagree with that because of the number of steps that people have to take to attest to their citizenship, to declare consistent with what is required by both federal and state law that they are citizens when they register to vote.”
He said it is California’s stance that “if the Executive Branch wants that authority in the first instance, they need to go ask Congress for it, they haven’t done that.”
He added: “They ask this court to short circuit the democratic process and issue an order, not just on the eve of an election, but as an election is underway.”
