articles.headline: Mass Effect's Commander Shepard Actors, Destiny Community Help #SaveMassEffect Petition Cross 200,000 Signatures
keyFacts: The #SaveMassEffect petition crossed 200,000 signatures after EA announced the closure of BioWare and the cancellation of Mass Effect 5.
Commander Shepard voice actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer publicly supported the movement and encouraged fans to sign the petition.
The Destiny community and other gaming figures also lent their support to help boost the petition's visibility.
body: The #SaveMassEffect movement has picked up even more steam after videos from both Commander Shepard actors – and even posts from the Destiny community – helped its petition reach 200,000 signatures.

It's been a whirlwind week for Mass Effect players and fans of the now-shuttered legendary RPG developer BioWare. After EA announced it would be closing the studio and canceling development for Mass Effect 5 , fans took action , and the result is something to behold.

In the first weekend of the #SaveMassEffect movement and its accompanying petition, more than 200,000 verified users have offered their signature to the cause. That's thanks in part to the wild amount of social media attention it's garnered in just a few days, but two of its most prominent supporters have already been backing Mass Effect for decades.
I like this thought…
#MassEffect #Femshep #broshep #N7 https://t.co/wnCS1I1w0u
— Jennifer Hale (@jhaletweets) October 24, 2026

"You know what I like to think about?" actor Jennifer Hale, who famously played the female version of Commander Shepard for the first three Mass Effect games, said in a video over the weekend. "I like to think about a world where the fans come together to create a Kickstarter, and then a couple of investors join them, and then a really cool game company joins them. Then a collective is formed to bring Mass Effect back to life for the community, for the creatives – for all of us – and it's amazing. That's what I like to think about."

It's a scenario that fans have pushed for, and one Hale believes in. She had already spoken out about the sadness surrounding BioWare's closure after a leaked trailer for its canceled Mass Effect: Universe project found its way online. At the time, she felt "weirdly hopeful," and just a few days later, she donned the #SaveMassEffect hashtag in a post .

When Hale first shared her feelings about EA's decision to lay off staff and bring the game side of the franchise to a halt , she wasn't alone. Joining her during an Instagram livestream was male Shepard actor Mark Meer. He echoed her thoughts, saying that it was "very sad news" for BioWare's home location in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and the industry as a whole. He returned to social media to share a similar video , #SaveMassEffect in tow.
I like it too.
Hold the line.
#MassEffect #SaveMassEffect #N7 #MassEffectIsAlive #CommanderShepard https://t.co/vx22yejYbR
— Mark Meer (@Mark_Meer) October 24, 2026
"I just saw my friend, Jennifer Hale, post about an idea, and I think it's a pretty good one," Meer said. "Save Mass Effect. Hold the line. I should go, and you should go… sign that petition."

At the time of this story's publication, the #SaveMassEffect petition on Change.org, which aims to "prominently illustrate to EA the significance of this iconic series" and demand it continue, has crossed the 200,000-signature mark. It's thanks in part to the continued signal boosting from notable figures like Hale and Meer, who may not have even been included in new Mass Effect games, but they aren't the only ones without a stake in the franchise's future who chose to speak up.

Destiny players, who did their own fair share of organizing when Sony moved to cease development of Destiny 2 content earlier this year, have been a vocal force in the aftermath of BioWare's closure. Although it's hard to say whether organization of this magnitude might impact any decisions to give BioWare developers and their ideas a path forward, the effort is a bit heartwarming to see.

Others from different gaming communities have also done their best to lend a hand. You don't have to search too hard to find posts encouraging anyone who's ever had a brush with Shepard's fight against the Reapers to lend their signature to the cause. Another significant helping hand arrived from developer Owlcat Games, which used the official X/Twitter account for its upcoming game, The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, to ask followers to consider signing the petition in a currently pinned post .

Last month, Destiny players were shocked to hear that Bungie was revisiting its plans for the franchise after its community spoke up . In general, revivals at this level are unlikely, and there's no telling if Mass Effect fans will be quite as lucky, but for now, fans don't seem to show any sign of stopping. While we wait to see what is, hopefully, next for the legendary sci-fi RPG series, you can learn more about Mass Effect: Universe thanks to some recently leaked gameplay details . articles.headline: Antonelli delivers 'the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet'
keyFacts: Kimi Antonelli won the United States Grand Prix, putting him on the brink of a record-breaking world championship.
Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff described Antonelli's victory as the best performance he has delivered so far.
Antonelli can secure the world championship in Mexico City next weekend unless George Russell or Lewis Hamilton wins the race.
body: - Published

The race that took Kimi Antonelli to the brink of a record-breaking world championship was, in the words of his Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff, "the best he has delivered so far" and "the race of a champion who isn't the champion yet".
Not yet. Not quite. But so very near.
The 20-year-old Italian's victory in the United States Grand Prix puts him in an impregnable position.

Antonelli is so far ahead in the points that the only way he could not win the title in Mexico City next weekend is if either his team-mate George Russell or Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton win the race. Even then, Antonelli will guarantee the title if he finishes ninth, or 10th if it's Hamilton.
He arrived here thanks to one of the most dominant victories of the season, in a car in which Russell could finish only eighth, albeit hampered by a five-second penalty.
While Russell was toiling and failing to pass McLaren's Oscar Piastri, Antonelli was operating on another level entirely, as he has so often this season.
"Exceptional," Wolff said, "and I think he's outperformed the car."
Antonelli came to Austin already in a strong position in the championship, knowing he would clinch the title if he won with Russell finishing lower than eighth and Hamilton lower than fourth.
He achieved his part of the bargain but Russell and Hamilton did just enough to keep things alive until this coming weekend. Russell was eighth and Hamilton fourth.

Some drivers tighten up when they get this close to achieving their lifetime's ambition. Not Antonelli. He said he was going to treat this like any other weekend, but it wasn't just talk. It's exactly what he did.

"He comes in," Wolff told BBC Sport after the race, in a conversation after finishing his official news conference, "sits on my chair, feet up, and keeps chatting away and saying: 'This is so funny. I'm not thinking about the championship at all.' And in a kind of youngish excitement, almost like it's surreal. And that's why it's not so important."
Did Wolff think that was because Antonelli's lead was so large that he had no need to feel any pressure, or was it innate?
"The advantage helps," he said. "But it's also innate in him and I don't think that it's something to be trained for. He's not over-thinking it."
Wolff's claim about this being Antonelli's best performance so far might surprise anyone who watched him win his home grand prix at Monza from 19th on the grid.

When this was pointed out, Wolff replied: "My problem is that I don't remember past races. So now you're saying Monza was actually also pretty good, obviously with the advantage of the home crowd and seeing all these tifosi that were a little bit confused, wearing red, and an Italian with the Mercedes outfit up on the podium. And I think we're going to see more Kimi caps, Mercedes caps next year.
"So both of them were pretty good. But the headline that this is the best we can keep."

Antonelli agreed. "Monza, we clearly had the fastest car," he said. "We were just super quick, so of course it was incredibly special coming from the back. But it was also a track where it was relatively easy to overtake, and we were so quick.

"Definitely, Monza was a super-special one, and one that I will remember forever. But this one probably, in terms of execution, was better, because the way we built up and the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good."
Mercedes went to Austin with both cars in the new upgraded specification that had proved unconvincing, to say the least, when it made its debut in Malaysia two races ago.

There, Wolff said he thought it had made the car 0.3secs per lap slower. The team split the cars in Singapore to try to understand the package better, and then used it on both cars in Austin. Antonelli stuck it on pole and dominated the race. Russell's performance looked more like the one the car produced in Malaysia.
"The update we put on the car is difficult to operate," Wolff said. "And Kimi landed it.

"Maybe it's a bit harsh to say but I think his driving style just glues with the car. We saw that in qualifying yesterday where on his last lap he could have been another 0.15-0.2 secs up. And on the other side George just struggled so much. And I believe this is because the operational window of the car is so difficult."

When Antonelli clinches the title, he will become the first Italian to do so since Alberto Ascari in 1953. It's a remarkable statistic for a country which is so engrained in the sport, and it certainly resonates with his compatriots.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella said: "As an Italian, wow, we need to go back to Ascari, the names that they created the inspiration for all of us. To see an Italian achieving this level of performance and results in Formula 1, that's particularly thrilling, as an Italian person in motorsport."
Stella's answer continued into an area that begins to explain the way in which he has proved so superior to Russell this year.
"Going more into the technical, and specifically this season, Kimi is a very interesting one to look at, because he pretty much attacks all the times," Stella said.

"You see how often he's just going off track, and you see his onboard (camera), he's pretty aggressive. But at the same time, this seems to be not only kind of an aggressive driving, or an attacking driving, but effective.

"And if we think how much we talk in these media sessions about the cars being difficult to drive consistently fast, it should be recognised how much he's been able to harness his driving style with what is required of the cars.
"But at the same time, almost contradicting what I'm saying, when is the time to bring home the result, he's been able to do it.
"So he's the deserving leader of this championship. He's writing an important piece of history for motorsport, because once he achieves the championship, he will be the youngest."
Antonelli will beat by more than three years the previous record for youngest winner of the championship, Sebastian Vettel in 2010.
As with the title itself, he is aware of the forthcoming achievement, but not letting it affect him.
"I'm going to approach it with the same mindset," he said. "Just trying to have as much fun as possible, trying to hopefully fight for another win.
"It would be best to finish on a high, and that's the goal. But I'm just going to try to enjoy the rest of the season from now on."

articles.headline: The best apps for tracking your reading and discovering new books
keyFacts: TechCrunch compiled a list of book-related apps designed to help users track reading goals, organize lists, and discover new titles.
The featured applications include Fable, Bookshelf, Pagebound, StoryGraph, and Margins, which all offer various free and subscription-based features.
These platforms provide options for community discussions, AI-powered summaries, reading statistics, and mood-based book discovery.
body: From discovering new books and organizing your reading list to tracking your reading goal and sharing recommendations, book apps make it easier to maintain reading as a hobby. There are numerous apps on the market that promise to do just that, so we’ve compiled a list of some of the best ones to help you pick the right one for you. Whether you’re an occasional reader or a dedicated bookworm, these apps can help you make the most of your reading journey.

Some of the apps on this list are somewhat new, while others have been around for a few years. Amazon-owned Goodreads, which is arguably the most popular book-related app, isn’t included in this list because we’re focusing on newer, lesser-known platforms.
Fable

Fable is a reading app that combines book tracking with a social platform. It lets you organize reading lists, set reading goals, track streaks, write reviews, and join virtual book clubs. You also get personalized book recommendations and the chance to discuss what you’re reading with other readers.

The app differs from others on this list because it puts reading and community at the forefront of the platform, which makes it a great option for people who like staying motivated to read by being part of a community and discussing their reads.
Fable is free to download on iOS and Android, but also offers a Fable Plus subscription tier that unlocks additional features like custom goals and advanced analytics for a monthly fee of $5.99.
Bookshelf

Bookshelf is a reading app designed to help people organize their libraries, discover new books, and remember more of what they read. The app positions itself as an alternative to Goodreads, and combines traditional reading logs with AI-powered recommendations and tools.

You can create custom shelves, set reading goals, receive reminders, save favorite quotes, and access AI-generated book summaries, key insights, and thematic analyses to recall the books you’ve read and get a deeper understanding of them.
Bookshelf is free to download on iOS, but offers a $6.99 monthly fee to unlock premium features like unlimited collections and enhanced analytics.
Pagebound

Pagebound is a book app that lets readers track their books, create lists, set goals, and discuss individual titles in dedicated forums. Instead of having to join an actual book club group, users can post reactions and thoughts to connect with others reading the same title.

You don’t have to worry about spoilers for the end of the book, as conversations are organized based on reading progress, allowing readers to share theories and thoughts as they read. The app is a great option for people who want to discuss their reads with others without having to commit to a scheduled book club.
Pagebound is free to download on iOS and Android and offers a $9.99 monthly subscription for added features like profile customization.
StoryGraph

StoryGraph is a reading app that lets users track their reading, discover new books, and access detailed reading statistics and personalized recommendations. Users can set reading goals, join reading challenges, and find new titles based on their preferred moods, themes, genres, and pacing.

The app is ideal for readers who want to better understand their reading habits and discover books that match their current interests. Its recommendation system doesn’t solely rely on what’s popular or trending, and instead caters to exactly what readers are looking for.
StoryGraph is free to use on iOS and Android, but also offers a paid subscription called StoryGraph Plus that costs $4.99 per month and unlocks custom charts, additional statistics, and more.
Margins

Margins is a great option for mood readers, as it offers mood-based discovery alongside a more focused reading experience. It helps users find their next read based on how they feel in the moment by searching for specific vibes, such as “books like 1920s Paris.” Users can also track their reading goals.

The app also lets users customize their virtual library by choosing book covers that match their aesthetic and organizing their shelves in different ways, including by color. For users who enjoy a more immersive experience, Margins offers a built-in “Reading Time” meditation timer that blocks social media apps.

articles.headline: Phantom Blade Zero review: "A GOTY contender with combat that looks as good as it feels"
keyFacts: GamesRadar reviewer Luke Kemp called Phantom Blade Zero a Game of the Year contender, praising its combat, weapon design, and tightly designed world.
The reviewer stated that the action-adventure game features wuxia-inspired combat and a kungfupunk aesthetic, but suffers from inconsistent storytelling and pre-launch bugs.
After completing the 30-to-35-hour campaign and reaching the bad ending, the reviewer continued exploring the map to find secret bosses and the true ending.

A rich and carefully designed world hides plenty of secret bosses and powerful weapons, with combat that effortlessly strikes down most of its peers. With fights that feel great and flow smoothly, Phantom Blade Zero proves itself as one of the best action-adventures of the year.
Reasons to buy

Phantom Blade Zero is not a Soulslike. This needs to be the first thing that I tell you, because you need to wipe away any such preconceptions in order to fully appreciate what it is (and is not) doing. The intricate combat and hostile land come instead from wuxia storytelling traditions, and a supernatural martial arts world that can be traced back to the director's first game Rainblood: Town of Death. While "very, very good" is not a genre, it's certainly an accurate description of this game.

Following the events of a prologue I'm not allowed to tell you about, our hero Soul is left with just 66 days to live. This doesn't mean a Dead Rising style time limit – in-game time only passes after specific story beats – but it does mean that anybody feeling particularly brave can opt for a hardcore difficulty that wipes your progress after 66 deaths. That could potentially mean losing dozens of hours of play, so if you opt for that, consider yourself warned.
Why Trust GamesRadar+

Having already reviewed Nioh 3, Beast of Reincarnation, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword this year, I was well up for another sword-swinging adventure. Using a PC code from the publisher, I spent dozens of hours fighting my way through Phantom Blade Zero's world, finding that it offered me an experience that just about managed to beat them all. Just don't talk to me about the Memory Flowers. – Reviewer Luke Kemp

Developer S-Game is keen to celebrate what it calls a "kungfupunk" aesthetic. It's an appropriate turn of phrase. As I explore the Phantom Realm, meeting new people and chopping them up, I find characters and locations that subtly fuse nature, supernatural horror, Chinese history and mythology, and a hint of the modern world. I fight faceless warriors wielding blades, phantoms playing pipas, deformed monstrosities that could never be mistaken for human, and much more. All this across locations including cliffs, a lake, fields, villages, caverns, and a lavish estate.

Combat is at the heart of it all. And what combat! Every time I start a fight – which happens a lot – it's with a smile on my face. Every clash is a deadly dance between my opponent and I, and we both look like masters of the craft. Together, we weave graceful tapestries of blocks, swing, parries, lunges, dodges, and violently flamboyant strikes. Avoid button-bashing (which will usually see you punished anyway), and Phantom Blade Zero offers that rarest of things; combat that looks as good as it feels.

Visually, the combat owes much to S-Game's commitment to motion capture, including a number of martial artists. Hong Kong movie legend Donnie Yen (who you may know from the Ip Man series, or as Caine in John Wick: Chapter 4) is credited as Creative Consultant, and he even took part in some motion capture himself. It's not all relentless flailing, either, as enemies (particularly some of the tougher bosses) will sometimes size you up or wait for you to approach before striking.

Scraping away the impressive visual flourishes, I still manage to find one of the best combat systems I've come across in a long time. From the first few fights right up until the final boss, I sometimes catch myself thinking this just works so damn well. Yes there are parries, yes there are unblockable red-flash attacks, and yes weapons are upgradeable; but it doesn't quite feel like anything else in the best possible way. I block a series of attacks from a boss, yet can still get in a few hits of my own before they're finished. Failing a parry or a dodge, I'm punished ruthlessly. Next time, I just… stay out of range, then dive in with fists full of vengeance. Too often in other games, that's not even an option.

Then there are the weapons themselves, another stroke of genius. There are a total of 30 regular ones, most of which are entirely missable in the expansive world. Each and every one has some kind of unique trait, and gains even more as they level up (you equip two weapons at a time, switching between them instantly refilling the Sha-Chi depleted by blocking and strong attacks). An early one I stick with for over a dozen hours builds up bleed status in human enemies, while another comes with a jug of booze to induce Tipsy and Drunk states (don't drink and dice, kids). Some excel at breaking through shields, others can counter enemy attacks, and not a single one is a match for any other.
Sign up to the GamesRadar+ Newsletter
Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

Then there are the many Phantom Edges to find and use, limited-use weapons that might do anything from strike enemies from a distance to temporarily summon minions to your side. A small number feed into the light brush of Metroidvania to the experience, in that they can (without cost) be used to traverse or open up new routes in the world. On rare occasions this will be compulsory to advance the story, but usually, it simply allows me to sate my curiosity for a previously inaccessible area.

Finding where to use my new blocker-cracking goodies is nice and simple, as relevant areas are marked on the map automatically; and turn a pleasant shade of green when you have the corresponding Phantom Edge. In fact, despite the often challenging combat, Phantom Blade Zero does a lot to smooth your progress. Save/respawn points are (usually) placed very generously, medicines are refilled each time you come back to life, and – this is a biggie, and may prove a point of contention for some – enemies almost never respawn. Like I said, it's important to remember that this isn't a Soulslike.

Although Phantom Blade Zero has a huge map with multiple regions, it doesn't quite feel right to call it open world. For one thing, it's tightly designed and tightly paced, with almost no wasted space. Whenever I uncover a new area or decide to wander off the obvious path, there's always something to find (usually including something, or several somethings, that want me dead).

The main story drives me forward, with no doing laps of the same area or regular backtracking to well-worn paths. Nonetheless, I find exploring irresistible, and make a habit of wandering down routes that lead away from my next objective. I'm regularly rewarded for doing so. There's some traditional "collect four X to increase your Y", and in addition to this, the more I explore the more weapon upgrade materials I find. I stumble on many hidden bosses this way, too, laying my hands on powerful weapons I would have otherwise missed. Curiosity is, quite literally, good for my Soul.

I find the combat fantastic, exploration compelling, and the storytelling… inconsistent. There's quite a lot of it. There's in-game dialogue, traditional cutscenes, and a few more experimental approaches that I heartily applaud. There are also seemingly hundreds of notes scattered about all over the place, which I'm less a fan of. I'm usually happy to read in-game text, but there are far too many bits and pieces here, especially for an action game. I quickly adopt a habit of picking them up and then instantly exiting the text screen.
Bloke Zero
Accessory to murder

Don't neglect your accessories! Struggling with a boss fight? Try swapping in a new accessory or two, it could make a huge difference. There are ones out there that provide elemental damage resistance, increase damage against certain enemies, and boost your HP.

The worst offenders, for me, are the Memory Flowers. These contain some of the most crucial story details and are, in addition, tied into HP increases and unlocking some of the more powerful character skills. Whenever I Interact with one, Soul stands perfectly still, staring down at a blue flower while voices play in his head for a few minutes. I have the option of skipping through lines at least, but I stubbornly refuse. Doesn't that kind of defeat the point?

The storytelling ranges from the great to the weak, and while it's mostly pretty straightforward, some of it goes over my head a bit. It's more of a minor annoyance than anything else though, and so it says something that this is my greatest criticism of the game. I do run into a few bugs – two boss fights see me getting stuck on the scenery, resulting in me taking unavoidable damage which makes me say very naughty words – but these are relatively small ones that can and, hopefully, will be patched out on or shortly after launch.

After 30-35 hours, I reach the final boss and – eventually – emerge victorious. Of course I do. Look at how much I've buffed up Soul and his weapons! After all that time, and a great deal of chasing down sidequests and digging out secrets, I am rewarded with what is very definitively the Bad Ending. It's abrupt, and unsatisfying on a few different levels. Nonetheless, I'm surprised to find that I'm not too bothered. There's so much of the map I have yet to explore – including an entire region – I immediately dive back in, eager to see what I'll find next.

One of the things I find is that some secret bosses crucial to the True Ending represent a stratospheric difficulty increase. I'm not quite sure how I feel about this. I was doing so well up until then! But in the end, I decide I'm OK with it. After all, there's so much still to see and do, and I can't wait to see and do it.
Disclaimer
Phantom Blade Zero was reviewed on PC, with a code provided by the publisher.

Luke contributed regularly to PLAY Magazine as well as PC Gamer, SFX, The Guardian, and Eurogamer. His crowning achievement? Writing many, many words for the last 18 issues of GamesMaster, something he’ll eagerly tell anybody who’ll listen (and anybody who won’t). While happy to try his hand at anything, he’s particularly fond of FPS games, strong narratives, and anything with a good sense of humour. He is also in a competition with his eldest child to see who can be the most enthusiastic fan of the Life is Strange series.

articles.headline: After threatening AI export bans, China allows DeepSeek to keep selling
keyFacts: China's Ministry of Commerce revised export restrictions to require licenses for certain AI technologies while exempting open source software.
Chinese state media reported that AI companies DeepSeek and MiniMax received authorization to continue selling their products abroad.
The policy changes help Beijing build export industries and retain sovereign control over critical AI infrastructure.
body: China has proposed to restrict export of some AI technologies but quickly moved to allow some of its champion companies to continue shipping their wares abroad.

Beijing’s Ministry of Commerce announced the restrictions in mid-October by revising its Catalogue of Technologies Prohibited and Restricted from Export in China. The restrictions mean that Chinese companies must apply for a license to export their tech.

New entrants on the list included “23 technologies related to large-scale models, intelligent agents, computing clusters, and information processing.” Tech issued under open source licenses is exempt from the restrictions.
Last Friday, Chinese state media reported that two companies – named elsewhere as DeepSeek and MiniMax – received authorization to continue exports.
Both companies are credible challengers to American AI vendors, so letting them sell their wares abroad meets China’s goals of creating export industries and enhancing its tech sector.
The expanded Catalogue also gives Beijing the ability to stop exports of any AI it feels represents important sovereign capacity, such as tools that are potent bug-finders or have military uses.
China is not alone in restricting exports of AI technology: the USA has imposed on-again, off-again, bans on sales of advanced GPUs to China.
AI datacenter bubble wobbles in Australia
If the AI datacenter building bubble bursts, two recent Australian incidents may prove instructive.
The first took place on October 9, when a company called Firmus called off its initial public offering.

Firmus already operates four datacenters, two in Australia and a pair in Singapore. It plans several more, plus expansions of its existing bit barns. Meta has committed to spend over $700 million with the company. Private investors had already ploughed over $2 billion into the company.
The float would have been Australia’s largest for 20 years and aimed to raise around $5 billion, giving Firmus a valuation over $40 billion.

In the days before the float, investor sentiment suddenly soured. Would-be buyers reportedly asked Firmus to lower its share price and therefore valuation by perhaps a quarter, as they feared the company’s prospectus made very optimistic revenue predictions.
Not helping matters was that one of Firmus’ founders did time after being convicted of insider trading.
The company eventually cancelled its IPO.

The other incident took place on Wednesday, when established datacenter operator NEXTDC announced [PDF] reduced revenue forecasts because its chosen power supplier suspended work “because of community and stakeholder opposition.”

That opposition related to installation of poles and wires needed to bring juice to an existing datacenter NEXTDC intends to expand. Protestors have blocked access to the site, and the local council has decided not to allow the power company to use relevant roads while community consultation continues.

NEXTDC, which readers may recall designed one of its datacenters to resemble sets from Sean Connery flick The Hunt For Red October , slashed its revenue forecast and then saw its share price slump almost 40 percent. The company told investors it will be at least February before its power supplier can resume work.

Hyperscalers mostly use third party datacenters in Australia. The nation’s government wants to get a slice of the investment on offer during the AI boom but has also set rules requiring new builds to bring their own renewable energy supply and pay for any grid enhancement costs.
Canberra hopes that approach attracts sufficient interest that Australia ends up with onshore AI capacity that, even if it won’t be sovereign, will at least be local.
Grab suggests shopping data could detect disease
Singapore-based Grab, whose “super-app” offers rideshare, e-commerce, financial services, and more, has suggested the data it collects could help to detect outbreaks of disease.

“Retail purchases can supplement clinical surveillance because changes in demand for some over-the-counter products may appear before confirmed case reports,” the company wrote in a recent abstract, which raises the idea of tracking “changes in demand for products associated with symptoms, such as fever remedies or cough medicines.”
The company’s idea is to analyze customer behavior on its GrabMart grocery app, in the hope that doing so yields “an additional signal when demand changes across groups of symptom-related products.”
Grab is at pains to point out that it does not believe its data can detect disease alone, and that it has not deployed such a system. The company also calls for use of the smallest possible datasets.

“The analysis should use only eligible product categories, coarse geographic areas, and aggregate time windows approved for the stated public health purpose. It should not expose raw transactions or personally identifiable information,” the company suggested. Grab also says such monitoring must be government-approved, targeted to particular health concerns, and time-limited. It also acknowledges that the idea is a thought bubble that public health experts should assess before deployment.

“These applications should use aggregate trends only,” the company suggested. “The signal should not drive personalised medical advice, individual targeting, insurance decisions, or automatic changes to medicine search rankings.”
What could possibly go wrong?
South Korea to accelerate smart glasses privacy rules

South Korea’s science minister Bae Kyung-hoon has promised to accelerate development of regulation governing smart glasses, to address unauthorized filming and the potential for the devices to be misused in other settings such as during academic exams.

Speaking at a parliamentary forum, Bae said the government is already working on guidelines but plans to accelerate that effort, and that president Lee Jae Myung recently mentioned the need for regulation during a cabinet meeting.
The minister added that the guidelines will be developed at a “pan-ministerial level,” suggesting the effort will attempt to create comprehensive regulations.
IPO for India’s top telco vastly oversubscribed
Jio Platforms is India’s top telco, having won over half a billion customers since its 2015 launch, helped by low price subscriptions and own-brand handsets, plus clever content bundling.

The company will float this week by selling around a three percent stake in the company, and the IPO is likely to be rather successful as investors have expressed an interest to acquire 22 times more shares than the company will sell. Institutional investors are 70x oversubscribed.
The IPO values the telco at just over $100 billion and aims to raise around $3 billion. ®

articles.headline: Brazil's left-wing President Lula elected for fourth term
keyFacts: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff election, securing more than 51 percent of the vote for a fourth term, according to official results.
Lula defeated Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, who received more than 48 percent of the vote and said he would seek to annul the election result.
Lula said in a speech that the election was a defeat of denialism and lies, while Bolsonaro called the outcome inexplicable.
body: Brazil's left-wing President Lula elected for fourth term

BRASILIA, Brazil — In a stunning political comeback, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has been elected president of Brazil, according to official results from Sunday's runoff election, with more than 96% of the votes counted.
Lula secured more than 51% of the vote, defeating Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, who received more than 48%.

The result marks a historic moment in Brazil's democratic era. Since democracy was restored in 1989, no candidate who failed to win the first round of voting has gone on to win the presidency in the second round.

The victory also adds another chapter to Lula's long political career, securing him a fourth, nonconsecutive presidential term. Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, will be among the oldest sitting leaders in the Americas, alongside President Trump and Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega, both 80.
In a speech to ecstatic supporters in São Paulo, Lula said the election was a "defeat of denialism. A defeat of lies."

"I want to thank the Brazilian people for this generosity they have shown me for so long, to thank the youth who took to the streets to defend democracy, and the elders who went to vote," Lula told the crowd.
Lula's victory bucks a broader rightward shift across Latin America in recent years. In a pointed message to Trump, Lula declared that Brazil would not accept being "anyone's backyard."
A bitterly divided election

Election day unfolded chaotically. Around midday, Lula's campaign requested an extension of voting hours, arguing that some local governments had reduced bus services, making it harder for voters to reach polling stations. Bolsonaro also sought an extension, citing heavy rain in some states.
Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin extended voting by two hours, to 7 p.m., but some polling stations had already deactivated their electronic voting machines and could not resume voting.

Speaking briefly to journalists outside his home in Brasilia, Bolsonaro called the result "inexplicable" and said he would seek to annul the vote. "I will not give up on my Brazil, and I hope you won't give up either," he said.

Bolsonaro, 45, had campaigned on closer ties with President Trump and pledged to pardon his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for plotting a coup to overturn his 2022 election defeat to Lula.

Brazilians showed little enthusiasm for street campaigning in the early months. But Bolsonaro's first-round finish on Oct. 4 energized the contest, and in recent days supporters of both candidates have filled rallies and flooded social media in an effort to sway voters.
In the end, Lula's message of continuity and a focus on social spending prevailed.

"I think people woke up about the risk of a Bolsonaro government after the first round, and the mobilization made a difference," said Alessandra Miguel, a 35-year-old spa worker who voted for Lula in Rocinha, a favela in Rio de Janeiro.
From union leader to president

Lula rose to national prominence as the leader of a metalworkers' union that organized strikes that helped bring down Brazil's dictatorship in the 1980s. Unions and progressive Catholic activists joined forces at the time to form the Workers' Party, which Lula has now represented in seven presidential elections.

During Lula's first two terms in office, from 2003 to 2010, Brazil's economy boomed, and millions of Brazilians rose out of poverty. But many voters turned their backs on the party when Lula and other leaders became embroiled in corruption scandals in the 2010s. Lula himself was jailed, though his convictions were later overturned on procedural grounds.

On foreign policy, Lula has worked to boost the political influence of countries in the Global South as a founding member of the BRICS group, a grouping of major emerging economies that includes Brazil, China, Russia, India and South Africa. He has argued that Brazil should maintain friendly relations with all major world powers, though his ties with China and Russia have sometimes led him to clash with Washington.

Lula's approval rating rose after he stood up to Trump, but his disapproval rating remained higher than his approval rating at the start of the election season. Brazil's economic growth has been slower than during Lula's first two terms, and many Brazilians felt he had not done enough to address crime and public security.
During the campaign, Lula sought to address those concerns by proposing a ban on sports betting, announcing a debt renegotiation program and backing tougher penalties for minors who commit crimes.

He will govern a sharply divided country. Brazilian political scientist Jairo Nicolau, who studies presidential elections, said one of the most striking features of this year's contest was the rigidity of Brazilians' political allegiances.
Unlike in past years, Nicolau said, "people's identity of belonging to a tribe became more important than how they view different policy options."

articles.headline: Fitbit Air vs. Whoop: Which screenless fitness tracker is better for you?
keyFacts: Google introduced the Fitbit Air to compete with screenless fitness tracker market leader Whoop, which raised $575 million and reached a $10 billion valuation in March.

The Fitbit Air costs $100 for hardware plus an optional $100 per year for Google Health Premium, while Whoop operates on a membership model starting at $149 to $199 per year that includes the hardware.
The Fitbit Air is designed as a more affordable, user-friendly device for everyday users, whereas Whoop targets serious athletes with higher-end hardware and more granular data.
body: Fitbit Air vs. Whoop: Which screenless fitness tracker is better for you?
How locked in do you want to be?

Screenless trackers are all the rage right now, even though they've existed for decades. For instance, Whoop launched its first tracker in 2015, launching as among the first, if not the first of the category. In March, Whoop raised $575 million, garnering itself a $10 billion valuation, signaling increased interest in the space. But Whoop is now facing competition from companies like Garmin, Luna, Hume, Amazfit and, most notably, Google with its Fitbit Air (see our Fitbit Air review). In fact, Google teased it was preparing something like the Air on March 31 — the same day as Whoop's funding announcement. Whether or not the timing was coincidental, the Fitbit Air is quite obviously Google's take on Whoop and the category of screenless health trackers.

The Whoop MG is one of the company's newest, so it makes sense to compare that to the Fitbit Air. To determine which of these two is the better option for you, I've compared both devices on features and pricing. In short, they both do a great job of tracking activities, sleep, and vitals, and offering a comprehensive and informative app experience. But they also both require a subscription to get the most out of your data.
Key differences between them

The Fitbit Air is slimmer than Whoop bands, which has an impact on battery life. Newer Whoop models like the Whoop 5.0 and Whoop MG are rated to last 14+ days while Google says the Fitbit Air lasts up to seven. You can squeeze more hours out of the newer Whoop bands with a convenient wireless battery pack that you can slide onto the band to charge on the go. It adds bulk to your wrist but you never have to remove the band to recharge it as long as you keep the battery packed topped up.

The companion apps for both companies provide tons of data about activities, sleep and vitals. They also each have an AI assistant you can call on to log meals, ask for advice and even use to build a wellness and workout plan. But the Whoop app can be overwhelming at first. It's better suited to those who are serious about health, wellness and especially fitness, monitoring things like strain and recovery. Whoop also captures heart rate data at a higher sampling frequency. On the other hand, the Fitbit Air's Google Health app is more user-friendly for the average person.

While you can get away without a subscription with the Fitbit Air, getting just basic tracking, Whoop works on a membership setup and you can't use it without one. Sign up for a membership and the hardware is included. According to Whoop, "Whoop One will be sold on WHOOP 5.0 hardware in the US, MX, CA, EU and UK. WHOOP One in these regions will be sold at $199/ year." Outside of those regions, however, it's worth pointing out that the company says "Whoop One memberships are provided with a certified pre-owned 4.0 sensor and Onyx Superknit Band." If you have any issue with using pre-owned products, this might be of concern.

By contrast, the Fitbit Air comes with a three-month trial to Google Health Premium after which you can cancel or continue by paying a small fee. A Whoop membership starts at about $149 for the first year ($199 after the first year) or, for those already paying monthly, $25 per month. Meanwhile, Google Health Premium will set you back $100 per year (with an annual plan or $10 per month) on top of the hardware cost of $100.
The highest tier Whoop subscription is $359 annually! So, Whoop is better suited for serious athletes and the Fitbit Air for everyday users or casual fitness buffs.
Which should you buy?

The advantage with Fitbit Air is that even without a subscription, you still get basic health insights and activity tracking, including sleep tracking. What you miss out on is AI-driven features like the personal assistance, guidance, and training plans, along with access to workouts and deeper sleep insights. But if you're happy just to check in to see if you got a good's night sleep, how your vitals are and to log your daily walks and workouts, it's perfectly fine on its own. Plus, if you have a Google AI Pro or Ultra subscription, Google Health Premium comes as one of the perks.

Whoop's devices are higher-end, premium trackers, but there is no option to get one without a pricey membership. It has all the same sensors and the app works similarly, albeit with much more granular data about things like strain and recovery. Whoop even plans to offer in-app video consultations with licensed clinicians in participating locations. In my experience, I have noticed that Whoop is better at automatically detecting activities, which is useful for those who do strength training or intense cardio and don't want to have to manually start and stop a workout.

If you decide to pay for Google Health Premium with the Fitbit Air, that tracker offers a more engaging and conversational AI Coach experience. There is AI support with Whoop, but Google's version feels more natural, whether you want to tell it to log your coffee and oatmeal in the morning or advise about your sore shoulder and ask it to modify your training plan accordingly to accommodate. Overall, the Fitbit Air is the better and more affordable device for most people. But for those with deeper pockets who are undergoing intense training, a Whoop tracker might be worth it.

articles.headline: How to use J.O.O.N.A.S. in Moon Sweepers
keyFacts: Moon Sweepers players can purchase the endgame J.O.O.N.A.S. autonomous bot for twenty thousand dollars to clean lunar dust automatically.
Players must place the bot in desired cleaning areas and buy a nearby Capsule Catcher to process dust-filled capsules.
A single Capsule Catcher can handle dust from multiple bots as long as the bots are within range.
body: Moon Sweepers is all about cleaning the Moon and gather as much dust as possible, and using J.O.O.N.A.S. makes things ten times easier. Despite being part of the endgame, this autonomous bot is not only more efficient at cleaning the dust, but it does it all on its own.

This allows you to concentrate on other activities in your base and leave the menial task to the automation. However, setting it up can be slightly confusing if you don’t know what needs to be done. In this guide, I will explain the digital process of how the smart bot works.
How to set up J.O.O.N.A.S. in Moon Sweepers

First, you’ll have to purchase the bot from the Services tab. This one is an expensive purchase as each costs $20,000. Hence, do this only when you’re in the endgame and your base is fairly automated.

Screenshot by Destructoid Once you purchase J.O.O.N.A.S., place it where you want it to clean the surface. You can place it anywhere including areas that are harder to reach. It will then keep cleaning dust and send it back to your base. It moves and cleans automatically, which is the biggest reason why you should purchase it in the first place.

There’s another important piece of the puzzle. You’ll also need to purchase a Capsule Catcher. The J.O.O.N.A.S. uses capsules that are filled up with dust. Once a capsule is filled completely, the bot will shoot it out. To process the dust, you’ll need to use the Capsule Catcher.
Make sure that the Capsule Catcher is located close to where the J.O.O.N.A.S. A single catcher can be used by multiple bots as long as they’re in the range.
That’s all you have to know about J.O.O.N.A.S. It’s certainly one of the best tools to have to clean the Moon efficiently .

articles.headline: Data centre debate heats up ahead of US midterms - here's what you need to know
keyFacts: Data centres powering the AI boom are growing rapidly in size and number, sparking global public backlash over high electricity and water consumption.
In the US, data centres have become a major issue ahead of the November midterm elections, with politicians opposing them against President Donald Trump.
Supporters say data centres create jobs and boost the economy, while the tech industry plans to continue spending heavily on AI infrastructure.
body: Until a few years ago many of us may have been blissfully unaware of what a data centre was.
These giant, warehouse-like buildings power virtually all our internet activity, from our web searches and emails to movie downloads and online banking.
They are at the heart of the AI boom, housing the advanced computer chips and servers needed to run services like ChatGPT and Claude.
But the speed at which they're growing, the enormous amount of electricity they consume and concerns about their environmental impact are fuelling a public backlash around the world.
In the US, they've become a huge issue ahead of the midterm elections on 3 November, with both Republicans and opposition Democrats coming out against their development.
It's putting opponents of data centre expansion on a collision course with US President Donald Trump, who has dismissed the pushback as a "sick conspiracy", even as public anger grows.
Here's what you need to know about the data centre boom, and why opposition is growing.
They are growing rapidly
There are about 12,250 data centres around the world, according to Data Center Map, external, a company that tracks both operational and pre-operational sites.
That's up sharply from 2021, when there were around 8,000, external operational sites.
As the chart below shows, data centres are most densely clustered in the US which has 4,767 sites. It is followed by Europe, where the UK and Germany lead.

Data centres have typically been located near to cities where it's easier to access high voltage power lines or water resources for cooling. But as they get bigger, more are being built in rural areas.
But when it comes to actual capacity, the US is ahead by a much larger margin, with China in second place and Europe lagging far behind.
This gap is set to widen in the coming years, leading some to warn Europe risks missing out on the potential economic benefits of the AI boom, external.
They are getting bigger
Data centres vary wildly in size, ranging from ones that fit inside a garden shed to others covering vast expanses of land.

The world's largest operational data centre is widely reported to be one run by China Telecom in Hohhot, Inner Mongolia, covering an area of approximately one million square metres (10.7 million sq ft). That is equivalent to about 140 Fifa football pitches.
However, much larger sites are under construction as the graphic below shows.
All these sites are being built exclusively to provide the immense computing power needed to run AI services.
For instance, Colossus 2, which is part of the wider Colossus campus, will house hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips made by tech giant Nvidia.

It will also be used to train xAI's chatbot Grok. Elon Musk's company will use 41 methane gas turbines to help power the site, which activists say could "significantly increase" local air pollution, external. Local regulators say the turbines will meet air quality standards.
They use more electricity than France

The pressure data centres put on local resources has sparked increasing concern. These facilities can use significant amounts of water to cool their systems, which could lead to water shortages, some experts say.
Data centres worldwide are also thought to consume more electricity than the whole of France, as the chart below shows.
This growing hunger for power is driving up carbon emissions, analysis shows, while putting pressure on local grids, which some fear could push up energy prices.
With others worried about the noise data centres make and the space they take up, a public backlash is gathering steam.
Some 16 US states have proposed laws to ban or temporarily block new facilities, and it could be a key issue in November's midterm elections.
Outside the US, opposition to data centres has emerged in countries like Mexico, France, Indonesia and the UK.
But they can boost jobs
But supporters say data centres are critical to national security, and the development of AI.
They also say they are good for the economy, external, attracting investment, generating tax revenue and creating jobs in areas like construction.
A recent report by the Brookings Center, external suggests data centres do create local jobs, although fewer than industry advocates claim.
The type of data centre matters too. So-called hyperscale facilities - massive sites owned and run by tech giants like Amazon and Microsoft - have a bigger positive effect on jobs, it found.
But "colocation" facilities, which lease space to remote tenants without a local presence, brought fewer benefits.
As the debate over their merits intensifies, the data centre rollout continues.
This year, the tech industry is expected to spend a combined $765bn, external ($544bn) on AI infrastructure in 2026, with this topping $1tn next year.
But as concerns about the environmental impact grow, the tech industry is exploring alternatives.
One idea is to put data centres in space, external or on the Moon, where they could harness abundant solar energy.
Others predict that more AI processing could eventually be carried out by the hardware already inside our computers and smartphones, reducing the need for vast data centres altogether.

articles.headline: Fabian Hurzeler aims ‘one team’ dig at Liverpool as Reds record 16-year low during Brighton win
keyFacts: Liverpool defeated Brighton 2-0 with goals from Pascal Gross and Alexander Isak despite recording their lowest home possession in a league win since 2010.
Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler stated after the match that only one team tried to win and described the result as a missed opportunity for his side.
Brighton will next face Manchester City in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup in midweek.
body: Liverpool beat Brighton despite achieving an unwanted 16-year first at Anfield on Sunday.
The Reds clinched a 2-0 victory thanks to two goals in four minutes as they moved up to fourth in the Premier League .
Liverpool saw off Brighton on Sunday despite having a lot less of the ball Getty
Pascal Gross’ own goal was followed by Alexander Isak’s sixth league goal of the season to wrap up all three points.
However, the win came despite the visitors having the majority of the ball against Andoni Iraola’s side.
Liverpool’s possession was recorded at just 35.6 per cent, their second-lowest on record in a Premier League home win.
Meanwhile, it was their lowest in a league victory at Anfield since November 2010.
On that occasion, the Reds had 35.3 per cent of the ball in a 2-0 win over Chelsea .
Despite their lack of possession, Liverpool recorded four shots on target to their opponents’ one.
Hurzeler aims dig at Liverpool
Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler believes only one team ‘tried to win’, though, as he took aim at the hosts following the match.
Speaking at full time, the German claimed: “Everyone in the stadium saw that there was one team who really tried to create and try to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players.
“Everyone in the stadium felt there was a missed opportunity for us, because it’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored.
“Also, before they scored, we had one, two big chances and today I think it was just the difference that they scored, we didn’t score.
Hurzeler claimed only one team tried to ‘create and win’ the match Getty
“Overall I saw a team with a lot of good things to take away.

“I saw a team that really had the belief in our approach, that stuck to the match plan, that always kept going, and that is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today.”
Sunday’s setback ended an eight-match unbeaten run in all competitions for Brighton.
Prior to the defeat, they had not loss since a 4-3 reverse away against Chelsea on August 30.
It was also their fifth successive loss at Anfield, with Brighton winning in the fixture just once in the Premier League since their promotion in 2017.
The result sees the Seagulls remain third in the table, a point ahead of Liverpool.
Liverpool ended Brighton’s eight-match unbeaten streak Getty
Hurzeler will be hoping for a response from his side in midweek as they visit Manchester City in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup.
The two sides meet again in the Premier League at the Etihad Stadium just three days later.

articles.headline: Trump rallies for Mike Rogers – and Nicki Minaj’s derriere – in Michigan
keyFacts: Donald Trump held a rally in Michigan to support Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers.
Trump encouraged the crowd to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj during the event.
Trump defended previous comments he made about the physical appearance of various political figures.
body: Donald Trump reiterated his apparent love for buxom bums during a rally in Michigan on Sunday where he encouraged the crowd to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj’s behind.

Trump’s cheeky comments about Minaj’s derriere came as he explained his recent observation on the Republican Ohio senator Jon Husted’s rear end. Earlier in October, Trump said of the former college football player: “I don’t do this with men very often. I started examining his body, because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I looked and I watched up and down. I looked at his ass and I looked at the whole – and then I looked at his hands. Look at his hands. He’s got these, like, claws.
“You are a great athlete,” Trump also said to Husted. “Congratulations.”

Trump was speaking at the rally to support Mike Rogers, the Michigan Republican Senate candidate. The Michigan race between Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed remains neck and neck as both political parties scramble for control of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections. But he couldn’t resist his purported other favorite topic.

This afternoon, Trump said the media buzz about these comments was “fake news” neglecting the athletic context of his statements. Trump said he had just learned Husted was a college athlete when he was “looking at him up and down, and I’m studying him”.
Trump insisted his subsequent crack was “in fun”. “I said: I looked at his ass, and I’ve never done that with a man before. It’s true. Off the record, women yes, men no, OK.”
Trump then shouted out Minaj, who the New York Post said was donned in “head-to-toe Gucci” today. Minaj, the paper also reported, was seen walking with Trump after leaving Air Force One.
“By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before – Nicki Minaj,” Trump said, prompting celebratory woos from the crowd. “That’s hard to miss. That – stand up! That’s hard to miss.
“OK, I’m going to get back to my story, Nicki,” Trump continued following still more cheers. “I hope Nicki wasn’t insulted, but we love Nicki. She’s been with us for a long time.”
Trump made statements about Husted’s tush just over a week ago in Kentucky.

“I examined his ass,” Trump said of Husted, who was not at the event. “And then I looked at his shoulders. I looked at his feet. I looked at his hand. I looked at his jawline. Studied him. He’s got a jawline.
“I then patted him on the shoulder, and it was like a piece of steel. I’m still recovering,” Trump said.
Trump also recently praised the appearance of Ed Gallrein, theRepublican congressional candidate from Kentucky.

“I needed somebody good, and this guy walks through the door,” Trump remarked of Gallrein, in describing his efforts to find a replacement for anti-Maga incumbent Thomas Massie. “I said, look at this beautiful guy.”
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment about why Trump has been discussing others’ bodies.
Trump’s comments come amid criticism of his language style, which some have likened to grotesquerie.
During a Saturday rally for El-Sayed, Barack Obama joked about Trump’s White House renovation efforts.
“He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” the former president said.
Meanwhile, Trump said that the US-Canada trade war would soon be in America’s rear view.
“Canada has been ripping off the US for years. I had to do it,” Trump said of tariffs during the rally. “We’ll have that settled pretty soon. They’re willing to give us anything at this moment.”

articles.headline: 'The pace was rubbish' - Russell in blunt admission after Austin struggle
keyFacts: Mercedes driver George Russell finished eighth and 54 seconds behind race-winning team-mate Kimi Antonelli at the United States Grand Prix.
Russell admitted to Sky Sports F1 that his pace was rubbish and said he currently has no answers for his struggles in Austin.
Antonelli is set to clinch the world championship this weekend in Mexico after extending his lead over Russell to 123 points.
body: George Russell: Mercedes driver admits to 'rubbish' pace in United States GP after finishing almost one minute behind Kimi Antonelli

Mercedes driver finished seven places and 54 seconds behind dominant race-winning team-mate Kimi Antonelli after struggle in the W17 car; Antonelli poised to clinch the world championship this weekend in Mexico after growing lead over Russell to 123 points
Monday 26 October 2026 02:26, UK
George Russell admitted his pace in the United States Grand Prix was "rubbish", with the Mercedes driver at a loss to why he trailed race-winning team-mate Kimi Antonelli by such a large margin,

Russell finished 54 seconds behind the sister Mercedes in the 56-lap race in an eighth place that only just kept him in mathematical championship contention heading to this week's race in Mexico, where Antonelli is set to clinch the crown.

Russell had held his grid position of sixth through the race's first stint but dropped to eighth after serving a five-second penalty at his sole pit stop for an incident with Oscar Piastri in the opening lap, when he was judged to have gained an advantage over the McLaren by running off track and retaining position.

Russell subsequently spent the final 26 laps on the similarly one-stopping Piastri's tail but was unable to find a way back past the Australian driver.
Russell told Sky Sports F1: "The pace was rubbish. That's the long and short of it.
"The five-second [penalty] didn't help things and probably cost me two or three positions but the pace wasn't good enough when it needed to be."
Russell made no excuse for his lack of competitiveness and said he had no immediate answer for why his Austin weekend was such a struggle.
"Just not been quick enough," he added.
"I need to try and understand why that is. It's strange when you're so far off.
"Hopefully there are some answers somewhere but at the moment I don't have them."
What went wrong for Russell?
Antonelli's win was his ninth of the year and represented what Toto Wolff, Mercedes' team principal, believes was "the best race that he's delivered so far".

It was the first win for Mercedes upgraded car, which has taken time for the world championship leaders to get the best out of since the aerodynamic revisions debuted at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia at the start of October.
The team have said, however, that the changes have narrowed the car's optimum set-up window.
On Russell's weekend, Wolff said: "George just struggled so much. And I believe this is because the operational window of the car is so difficult.
"In Q2 he was there and thereabouts. Q3, it didn't work. He said, 'that goes on me'.

"And today in the race, I don't know, we got stuck behind Piastri, which looks a bit unfair why he didn't get past. It's the same engine, it's the same electric charging and deployment. But I'm going to see him now."
'He's not 54 seconds slower over a race distance'
Analysis from Sky Sports F1's Jenson Button:

"George has had a lot of tough races but also some great races and that's the thing that's really difficult to understand - how he's able to get the maximum out of that car on some tracks but not at others.

"Austin was difficult as he started so far down. He was in the pack and when you're in the pack, sometimes it's difficult to move forward. You're in the dirty air. You try to do something different with strategy but then you get a five-second penalty which puts you back further.

articles.headline: iFixit’s look inside the iPhone Duo may explain those broken screens and hinges
keyFacts: Repair site iFixit gave the iPhone Duo a 5 out of 10 repairability score, making it the highest score given to a foldable device.
iFixit found that a matte nano-texture cover and specially angled subpixels help mask the screen crease on the iPhone Duo.
iFixit suspects that a complex hinge, an accordion cable, and pressure near the battery may explain reports of cracked screens.
body: As is tradition, iFixit has torn open the latest iPhone and laid its parts bare on a table. It found some interesting details about how Apple might be hiding the crease on the Duo’s folding screen and gave it a 5/10 repairability score. That might not seem particularly high, but it’s the best score the site has given to a foldable yet.
iFixit’s look inside the iPhone Duo may explain those broken screens and hinges
The iPhone Duo is the most repairable foldable yet, but that’s not saying much.

The internal screen’s matte nano-texture cover doesn’t just make it more readable in bright sunlight; it also helps mask the crease by scattering reflections. When looking at the display under a microscope, iFixit also found oval-shaped subpixels arranged at various angles, which the site believes are designed to reduce artifacts and further mask the crease down the middle of the display.

The nano-texture outer layer is relatively easy to replace without swapping out the OLED underneath. If you do need to repair the display itself, however, good luck. As is the case with other foldables, it’s an expensive nightmare. Dust did make it into the USB-C port, speaker grills, and the hinge — making it a bit crunchy. But noticeably less of the glow dust found its way inside the phone than the Z Fold8 or Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

As for reports of damaged screens and cracking hinges, iFixit has some theories. The hinge on the iPhone Duo is incredibly complex, and they suspect part of it sometimes isn’t descending properly. There is also an accordion cable that passes over that exact spot, and it’s near the edge of the battery. It’s possible this is concentrating pressure and leading to the “audible crack” reported by some and the broken screens. Apple did not immediately return a request for comment.

articles.headline: 187K+ fans call for EA to "Save Mass Effect"
keyFacts: A petition demanding continued development for the Mass Effect franchise has surpassed 187,000 signatures following BioWare's closure.
Petition organizer Joe Smith called on EA to properly fund the franchise or license the intellectual property to another studio.
The petition follows recent widespread job cuts by EA that also affected developers at Respawn, Maxis, and other studios.
body: A petition created to save BioWare's well-loved sci-fi RPG, Mass Effect, has topped 187,000 signatures.

We said a sad farewell to BioWare earlier this week. Job cuts, coming just months after Saudi Arabia's $55bn leveraged buyout of the company, were anticipated by experts, but drew widespread condemnation and messages of sympathy from across the industry.

Joe Smith, credited with starting the petition, isn't necessarily asking EA to change its mind about BioWare; instead, the petition calls for "decisive action by committing to the continued development of Mass Effect".
"This commitment requires proper funding, adequate staffing, and time allocation to maintain and advance the high standards the franchise is known for," the Change.Org page reads.
"Alternatively, EA could consider licensing the Mass Effect intellectual property (IP) to another studio that shares the passion and vision to keep it alive and allow it to flourish anew."

The petition adds: "Fans around the globe have invested thousands of hours exploring the galaxy, forming deep connections with its multifaceted characters and compelling storylines. It is a franchise that has transcended the typical gamer experience, creating a community that advocates for choice, individuality, and shared adventure. The potential cessation of new developments in this universe is a devastating prospect not only for fans but for the diversity of narrative-driven games as a whole."
Yesterday, we reported that a content creator claiming to have served on a BioWare community council shared alleged details about the cancelled next Mass Effect game, titled Mass Effect Universe.

In a lengthy Twitter/X post, the YouTuber claimed he'd had access through his role on the "Mass Effect Council", had seen firsthand what BioWare was developing, and had provided feedback during development.
This follows the appearance of an internal trailer for Mass Effect Universe, which BioWare later confirmed was real after the company’s closure and the game's cancellation.
EA's widespread job cuts also hit developers at Respawn, Maxis, Full Circle, EA Motive, and other EA-owned studios.

articles.headline: 'Grossly Incompetent': Trump Loses It Over Obama, El-Sayed In Early Morning Meltdown
keyFacts: President Donald Trump criticized former President Barack Obama on social media after Obama campaigned for Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed.
Trump insulted Obama's presidency and launched attacks against El-Sayed, while endorsing Republican candidate Mike Rogers.
Obama had previously criticized Trump during a Michigan rally and addressed attacks on El-Sayed's background.
body: President Donald Trump flipped out on his predecessor Barack Obama early Sunday morning after he attacked his administration while campaigning for Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for a U.S. Senate seat in Michigan.
“Obama was a grossly incompetent President!” began Trump in a 12:42 a.m. post to his Truth Social platform.

“He paid off Iran with $Billions, and gave them a road to a Nuclear Weapon. He said that Crooked Hillary Clinton was going to WIN, he campaigned hard for her, and she lost in all directions and ways. He then campaigned full out for Kamala, and likewise, she lost.”

Trump proceeded to turn to Islamophobic attacks to refer to El-Sayed, writing, “Now he’s campaigning for a Muslim Brotherhood Jihadist, who hates Jews and Blacks and AMERICANS and TRUMP, and he is going to lose, also. He’s a Fake Doctor, who runs what is considered to be the WORST CLINIC IN AMERICA.”

“I won Michigan, BIG, have brought back the Car Industry, the Air Force Base, and everything else. Also, more jobs than ever before. Michigan doesn’t want an arrogant, Open Borders, Fake Doctor, Jihadist, whose reputation will only get worse as more information is revealed - And there’s plenty. VOTE FOR MIKE ROGERS! He will never let you down! President DONALD J. TRUMP.”

The post arrived just hours after Obama — in one of his first rallies for this year’s midterms in Michigan, one he also used to back Michigan gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson (D) — slammed Trump’s “corruption,” “cruelty and chaos” and called out the “foolishness” of his administration.

Elsewhere, he appeared to tie attacks hurled at El-Sayed — whose Muslim identity and background has been a focus of his GOP opponent Mike Rogers — to those he faced from Trump through his racist “birther” conspiracy theories.

“Whenever a movement builds to challenge that broken system, the people who benefit from the status quo will say and do anything to stop that train from coming,” he said. “They will use lies and they will use fear and they will use division. And they may even use your name to suggest that you are dangerous and less than trustworthy and less patriotic and less American than they are.”

He emphasized, “We have seen this movie before. I starred in it. I’ve got a long form birth certificate to prove it. This stuff didn’t work on me, not in Michigan. It’s not going to work on Abdul. He is as Michigan as it gets. Abdul was born here. He was raised here.”

articles.headline: Is the Ninja MultiPot the Kitchen Appliance You Need, or Just the One You Want?
keyFacts: Ninja recently released the 12-in-1 MultiPot XL, a $250 countertop appliance featuring a 7.5-quart Megazone or two smaller 3.5-quart pots.
Testing showed the MultiPot XL excels at searing, sautéing, and boiling, but its slow cooker function produced less impressive results than a traditional Crockpot.
The reviewer stated the MultiPot XL is a good option for those with limited space who want a versatile appliance, though not a strict necessity.
body: When I think of kitchen brands dominating home kitchens and wishlists alike, Ninja immediately comes to mind.

Beyond the company’s viral social media videos and massively popular product releases, like the Crispi air fryer and Creami frozen dessert maker, the brand’s popularity may also be rooted in its rapid product launches. Ninja releases products fast, and it releases a lot of them.

In the last couple of months alone, we’ve seen the release of the Prepi, CrushBoss, NeverQuit cookware and now, the MultiPot XL. With colder weather setting in, the 12-in-1 cooker caught my eye. Theoretically, it can reduce kitchen clutter by replacing numerous other countertop appliances, but is it truly a worthy replacement for your Instant Pot, Crockpot and even the classic Dutch oven?

With so many new releases, how do you separate want from need? We cooked numerous meals with the new MultiPot XL to see whether the shiny new appliance has what it takes to earn a place on your countertop.
Searing, sautéing and soups
The Ninja MultiPot XL has 12 functions and the option to cook in the “Megazone,” a 7.5-quart pot, or in two smaller pots, each 3.5 quarts. All of the pots are ceramic-coated.
The first meal I cooked in it was homemade ramen, and I learned there are a few settings where the MultiPot excels, including the sear/sauté function.

The first ingredient I sautéed was mushrooms with butter. The MultiPot quickly preheated and sauteed the mushrooms just as well as a non-stick pan on a stovetop would. When the lids are shut, the pot quickly gathers steam to help speed up the cooking process too.

Next, I placed the chicken thighs in the already heated pot, and they took only a few minutes to cook all the way through. The best part was that the chicken developed a crust, which added extra flavor to the dish.
I used the same function for a handful of additional ingredients, combined everything in the pot with chicken broth and then set the MultiPot to its hot pot setting until everything came to a boil.

Because the pot was already hot, it didn’t take long to boil. When I was ready for it to stop, I turned off the appliance and lifted the pot off the hot plates so it wouldn’t overcook. Over the next couple of weeks, I continued to use the appliance for various meals, but sauté/sear and hot pot remained among my favorite functions.
It’s not a slow cooker replacement

Despite its ability to sear and sauté just as well as a non-stick pan on the stovetop, one setting was less impressive. I used the slow cooker setting to cook a small batch of beef short ribs in one half of the cooker, cooking them on low for over 8 hours. I’ve cooked this meal before in a slow cooker, and by the end of the 8 hours, the meat is usually falling apart and my whole house smells like the dish.

With the MultiPot, though, although the meat was still fully cooked through and had a great flavor, it wasn’t fall-off-the-bone cooked. I’m not entirely sure why that is, but it made me wish I’d cooked that dish in my Crockpot instead.
On the other side of the MultiPot, I cooked brown rice, and it cooked just as well as on the stovetop.

In my experience, the only place where the MultiPot has a leg up on a slow cooker is the fact that you can sauté or sear directly in the MultiPot, then turn the pot to the slow cooker setting, instead of having to sear in a separate pan on the stovetop, then transfer the ingredients to a slow cooker. So, if you’re looking for convenience, the MultiPot offers it.
Who’s the Ninja MultiPot XL best for?

If you have limited countertop space for appliances and want just one that can handle many cooking tasks, the MultiPot XL would be a great option. With 12 settings, it has more versatility than many competitors, but keep in mind that the “keep warm” function is included in the 12, and some functions won’t be used as much as others, such as sous vide.

At $250, it’s more expensive than standard slow cookers and Instant Pots, but it could be a good option if you often cook large meals for a group. If you’re looking for a cheaper multicooker, but want to stay in the Ninja family, the 8-in-1 Ninja PossibleCooker may be a smarter buy since it’s less than half the price but still has the essential functions. However, I haven’t tested the PossibleCooker myself.
The MultiPot XL can definitely be a great choice for some, but I wouldn’t put it in the must-have category, even if the rose quartz option is one of the cutest appliance color schemes I’ve seen.

articles.headline: A 1,000-mile cloud on Mars may reveal physics never seen in nature
keyFacts: A 1,000-mile cloud forms and disappears near the Martian volcano Arsia Mons every morning during spring and summer.
Scientists recently modeled the cloud's formation for the first time using computer simulations.
Study lead author Jorge Hernández-Bernal said the results suggest the cloud is driven by theoretical physics never before observed in nature.
body: Every morning during the Martian spring and summer, a thin and extremely long cloud emerges, only to disappear again. The wispy formation appears near the volcano Arsia Mons and gradually elongates until it reaches over 1,000 miles—about the distance from New York to Kansas City as the crow flies—before dissipating. This cycle then repeats for several months.

Since it was first recorded by a probe in 2018, scientists have been unable to find a plausible explanation for the existence of this cloud, often referred to as the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC). Until now. Recently, researchers successfully modeled the cloud’s formation for the first time, their results suggesting that it may be driven by a physical process that has never been directly observed in any planet's atmosphere.

"We found that we needed to include some exotic physics… physics that, while included in textbooks, is treated as theoretical and usually thought not to happen in nature. It certainly hasn’t been seen in action before," Jorge Hernández-Bernal, a planetary scientist at Paris’ Sorbonne Université and lead author of the study, said in a press release . "Once we included this physics in our simulations, the AMEC emerged just as we hoped.”
